question: A community nurse visits a village where the mother of an ill child tells her that eight persons have loose stools and vomiting within a day of a feast at the temple. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Record the cases in the register and report to the officer at the end of the month
option_2: Give a tablet for the vomiting to every person in the village at once
option_3: Close the village well and ask every family to use river water
option_4: Give oral rehydration solution to the ill persons and send a stool sample to the laboratory
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Give oral rehydration solution to the ill persons and send a stool sample to the laboratory

Clinical Rationale: Loose stools and vomiting in many persons after a common feast point to a food-borne illness, so oral rehydration solution is given to the ill persons and a stool sample is sent at once.

Key Clue: eight persons in a village with loose stools and vomiting within a day of a feast at the temple

Priority Principle: Public health / Outbreak

Why Not Others: (a) A report at the end of the month lets the illness spread through the houses; (b) A tablet for every person does not replace the fluid that is lost; (c) The well is not the cause when the food of the feast is the common item.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the village water seems the cause of every illness.

5-Second Recall: Ek hi bhoj ke baad sab ko dast-ulti = ORS do, stool lab bhejo, turant report.

PNC Exam Pearl: In an outbreak the cases are treated and the sample is sent on the same visit.

question: A 45-year-old man is brought to the clinic after a dog bite on the leg, and the wound is bleeding with torn skin. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Apply antibiotic powder and bandage the wound tightly
option_2: Tie a tight band above the wound to stop the bleeding
option_3: Wash the wound with soap and running water for a full fifteen minutes
option_4: Record the bite in the register and send the man home for a day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Wash the wound with soap and running water for a full fifteen minutes

Clinical Rationale: A dog bite is washed at once with soap and running water for about fifteen minutes, because washing removes the virus from the wound before the vaccine is started.

Key Clue: 45-year-old man with a dog bite on the leg and a bleeding wound with torn skin

Priority Principle: Wound care / Rabies

Why Not Others: (a) Powder and a tight bandage keep the wound from draining; (b) A tight band holds the virus inside the wound; (d) A wait of a day lets the virus travel towards the nerves.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tight band seems the sure way to stop the bleeding.

5-Second Recall: Kutte ka kaata = sabun aur behte paani se 15 minute dhoyo, phir vaccine.

PNC Exam Pearl: The wash matters more than any medicine in a bite of this kind.

question: A 25-year-old woman brings her 9-month-old child to the sub-centre and says the child has had no vaccine since birth. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Send the mother home and ask her to come after three months
option_2: Give the vaccines due for the age today and fix dates for the missed doses
option_3: Give only the polio drops and ask her to come for the rest later
option_4: Tell the mother that the vaccines of the early months are of no use now
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give the vaccines due for the age today and fix dates for the missed doses

Clinical Rationale: A 9-month-old child who has had no vaccine is started on the doses due for the age today and the missed doses are fixed on dates, because the schedule can be made up.

Key Clue: 9-month-old child with no vaccine since birth, brought to the sub-centre by the mother

Priority Principle: Health promotion / Immunisation

Why Not Others: (a) A wait of three months takes the child further away from the schedule; (c) The drops alone leave out the vaccines due for the age; (d) The early doses are of use even when they are given late.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a late start seems a wasted start.

5-Second Recall: Sahi umar ke saare vaccine aaj do, chhoote hue doses ki tareekh fix karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A missed dose is started at once and never written off.

question: A community nurse visits a village where a mother reports that the hand pump stands close to a drain and many families take water from it without boiling. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the families to boil the water and repair the drain with the village
option_2: Ask the families to take water from the river till the pump is moved
option_3: Give a drug for the loose stools to the children of the houses
option_4: Record the state of the pump and report to the officer after a month
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Tell the families to boil the water and repair the drain with the village

Clinical Rationale: Water taken from a pump close to a drain carries germs, so the families are told to boil the water and the drain is repaired with the village at once.

Key Clue: hand pump of a village close to a drain with families who take the water unboiled

Priority Principle: Public health / Safe water

Why Not Others: (b) The river may be no safer than the water of the pump; (c) A drug for the children does not clean the water they drink; (d) A month of waiting lets the loose stools go on in the houses.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a drug for the children seems the fast end of the illness.

5-Second Recall: Pump ke paas nala aur bina ubaale paani = ubaalne ko kaho, nala theek karao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean water stops the cases that a drug can only treat.

question: A community nurse visits the village where a family has asked that the water of the well be made safe for drinking, and the bleach powder of the health centre gives 25 per cent available chlorine. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put the whole packet of powder into the well and leave it for a day
option_2: Work out the amount of powder needed for the volume of the well and check the free chlorine
option_3: Ask the families to pour the powder into their pots without any measure
option_4: Take the water to the laboratory and wait for the report before any powder is put
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Work out the amount of powder needed for the volume of the well and check the free chlorine

Clinical Rationale: The amount of bleaching powder is worked out for the volume of the well and the free chlorine is checked, because an unmeasured dose is either useless or harmful.

Key Clue: a well of a village to be made safe with bleach powder of 25 per cent available chlorine

Priority Principle: Public health / Disinfection

Why Not Others: (a) A whole packet puts far too much chlorine in the water; (c) Powder poured without a measure gives an uncertain dose; (d) The wait leaves the families drinking water that is not yet safe.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a large dose of powder seems safer water.

5-Second Recall: Bleach powder ka hisaab volume ke hisaab se - khurak tol kar daalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The free chlorine of the water is checked after the powder is put in.

question: A 35-year-old man is brought to the clinic with a fever of 39 degrees Celsius, severe pain behind the eyes and pain in the joints and muscles. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Send the blood for the test of the germ and give fluid and a drug for the fever
option_2: Give a tablet of aspirin for the pain and ask him to rest
option_3: Ask the man to take a walk and come back after two days
option_4: Put a wet cloth on the head and note the fever in the register
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Send the blood for the test of the germ and give fluid and a drug for the fever

Clinical Rationale: A fever with pain behind the eyes and pain in the joints points to a mosquito-borne fever, so the blood is sent for the test and fluid and a drug for the fever are given.

Key Clue: 35-year-old man with fever of 39 degrees Celsius, pain behind the eyes and joint pain

Priority Principle: Public health / Fever of the village

Why Not Others: (b) Aspirin raises the risk of bleeding in a fever of this kind; (c) A walk through the village spreads the illness to others; (d) A wet cloth alone does not find or treat the cause.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tablet for the pain seems the whole care of the fever.

5-Second Recall: Bukhar aur aankh ke peeche dard = dengue ki jaanch, aspirin nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fever with pain in the joints is tested before any drug for the pain is given.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 50-year-old man is brought to the clinic with a wound on the foot that has a black edge and a foul smell, and the family says he has had the same dressing for a week. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Cut the black edge of the wound with a blade and wash it
option_2: Wash the wound with the water of the pump and dress it again
option_3: Give a tablet for the pain and ask him to come after a week
option_4: Send the man to the health centre at once for care of the wound
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Send the man to the health centre at once for care of the wound

Clinical Rationale: A wound with a black edge and a foul smell is dead flesh that needs care at a centre, so the man is sent at once.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man with a wound on the foot with a black edge and a foul smell and the same dressing for a week

Priority Principle: Wound care / Referral

Why Not Others: (a) Cutting the wound at home spreads the infection; (b) Washing with the water of the pump adds more germs to the wound; (c) A wait of a week lets the dead flesh spread up the leg.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a fresh dressing seems the whole care of the wound.

5-Second Recall: Kaala kinara aur badbu wala ghaav = turant health centre bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A wound with dead flesh is sent for care and not dressed at home.

question: A mother in a village gives sugar water with salt of her own measure to her 1-year-old child who has loose stools, and the nurse notes that the child is thirsty with dry lips. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a drug for the loose stools and ask the mother to wait
option_2: Stop all fluid and give the child plain water in small sips
option_3: Make the salt and sugar solution by the standard measure and give it to the child
option_4: Ask the mother to give the child only buffalo milk
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Make the salt and sugar solution by the standard measure and give it to the child

Clinical Rationale: A solution mixed by eye may hold too much salt, so the standard measure of the salt and sugar solution is made and given to the child at once.

Key Clue: 1-year-old child with loose stools, thirst, dry lips and a home-made salt and sugar drink of the wrong measure

Priority Principle: Dehydration / Fluid

Why Not Others: (a) A drug for the stools does not replace the water that is lost; (b) Plain water alone does not replace the salt that is lost; (d) Plain milk alone does not treat the loss of water and salt.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because plain water seems the safe fluid for a child.

5-Second Recall: Ghar ka namak-cheeni ka ghol anumaan se galat - standard ORS banao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The measure of the salt matters as much as the giving of the fluid.

question: A community nurse who visits the school finds a child of 8 years with an itchy scalp and small white nits on the hair. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Look at the heads of the other children of the class and treat the child
option_2: Send the child home and ask the parents to shave the head
option_3: Give a tablet for the itch to the child for a week
option_4: Note the finding in the school register and see the child next month
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Look at the heads of the other children of the class and treat the child

Clinical Rationale: An itchy scalp with nits spreads from head to head, so the other children of the class are examined and the child is treated at once.

Key Clue: 8-year-old child in a school with an itchy scalp and white nits on the hair

Priority Principle: School health / Infection

Why Not Others: (b) Sending the child home without care does not stop the spread; (c) A tablet for the itch does not remove the nits from the hair; (d) A wait of a month lets the nits spread in the class.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a child sent home seems the way to stop the spread.

5-Second Recall: School me sir ki jui = poore class ke sir dekho, ilaaj turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: In school health the whole class is examined and not the child alone.

question: A woman of 25 years and her husband in a village have children of 2 years and 4 years and ask the nurse how to wait for the next child. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Tell the couple that no method is needed till the third child is born
option_2: Tell the couple about the safe ways of spacing and help them to choose one
option_3: Ask the woman to take a tablet to stop the pregnancy
option_4: Send the husband alone to the health centre for the operation
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Tell the couple about the safe ways of spacing and help them to choose one

Clinical Rationale: The couple is told about the safe ways of spacing children and is helped to choose the method that fits their wish.

Key Clue: couple in a village with children of 2 and 4 years who ask how to wait for the next child

Priority Principle: Health promotion / Spacing

Why Not Others: (a) A wait without a method brings an unplanned pregnancy; (c) A tablet to stop a pregnancy is not a method of spacing; (d) The choice is made by the couple together and not by the husband alone.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because no method seems the simple answer for a young couple.

5-Second Recall: Do bachche aur agla intezaar = spacing ke saare tareeke batao, unki pasand poochho.

PNC Exam Pearl: Spacing is chosen by the couple from the methods that are offered.

question: A community nurse reads the test report of a 28-year-old woman of the village and sees that the germ of a blood-borne disease is present, and the woman's husband asks about the report. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the neighbours so that the house is helped by the village
option_2: Show the report to the husband because he is the head of the family
option_3: Keep the report private and tell the woman before any word is said to others
option_4: Note the report in the village register where all the families can see it
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the report private and tell the woman before any word is said to others

Clinical Rationale: A report of a germ that is spread by blood is the private matter of the woman, so it is kept private and the woman is told before any other person hears it.

Key Clue: a report of a blood-borne germ in the hand of the nurse and a husband who asks about it

Priority Principle: Ethics / Privacy

Why Not Others: (a) Telling the neighbours brings shame and drives the illness under cover; (b) A report cannot be shown to the family without the wish of the woman; (d) A register open to the village breaks the privacy of the woman.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the head of the family seems the person who must know.

5-Second Recall: Report pehle client ko, ghar walon ko uski marzi ke bina nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The report is spoken of with the client first and with others only by her wish.

question: A mother brings her 2-year-old child to the community nurse and says the child has had a cough for four days with fast breathing and vomiting after every feed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the worms and advise a soft diet for the child
option_2: Give a syrup for the cough and ask the mother to come after three days
option_3: Tell the mother that a cough of four days is common in winter
option_4: Look at the chest for drawing in and send the child to the health centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Look at the chest for drawing in and send the child to the health centre

Clinical Rationale: A cough with fast breathing and vomiting after feeds points to an infection of the lungs, so the chest is examined for drawing in and the child is sent to the centre at once.

Key Clue: 2-year-old child with a cough for four days, fast breathing and vomiting after the feeds

Priority Principle: Child health / Infection of the lungs

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet for the worms has no part in a cough with fast breathing; (b) A cough syrup and a wait of three days let the infection grow; (c) Fast breathing is not part of a simple cough of winter.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a cough of winter seems a small matter.

5-Second Recall: Khansi aur tez saans = chest dekho, turant health centre bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fast breathing with a cough in a small child is treated as an infection of the lungs.

question: A community nurse who visits the village notes that there have been four cases of a fever with bleeding from the gums within a week, and a family has stored water in open pots near the house. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the fever to every person of the four houses
option_2: Report the cluster of cases at once and begin the work against the mosquito
option_3: Wait for the blood reports of the four cases before any report is sent
option_4: Advise the families to keep the windows of the houses open
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Report the cluster of cases at once and begin the work against the mosquito

Clinical Rationale: Four cases of fever with bleeding within a week is a cluster that is reported at once, and the work against the mosquito begins on the same visit.

Key Clue: four cases of fever with bleeding from the gums in a week with open water pots near the houses

Priority Principle: Public health / Cluster of cases

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet for every person does not stop the mosquito that carries the germ; (c) A wait for the reports lets the cases grow in the village; (d) Open windows do not remove the water in which the mosquito breeds.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a drug for all seems the fast end of the illness.

5-Second Recall: Ek hafte me chaar bukhar-masoode se khoon = turant report karo, machhar ke khilaaf kaam.

PNC Exam Pearl: A cluster of cases is reported before the blood reports come.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 25-year-old woman in the 32nd week of pregnancy is brought to the clinic with sudden bleeding from the birth passage and a pulse of 110 per minute. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Send the woman to the hospital at once with fluid running into a vein
option_2: Do a look inside the birth passage to find the cause of the bleeding
option_3: Give a warm drink and let the woman rest in the bed of the centre
option_4: Wait for the doctor of the centre and note the amount of blood
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Send the woman to the hospital at once with fluid running into a vein

Clinical Rationale: Bleeding from the birth passage late in pregnancy with a fast pulse requires IMMEDIATE transfer to the hospital with an intravenous line running, because the cause is found and treated only there.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman in the 32nd week of pregnancy with sudden bleeding and a pulse of 110

Priority Principle: Bleeding / Mother and fetus

Why Not Others: (b) A look inside the passage can set off much heavier bleeding; (c) Rest in the bed of the centre leaves the heavy bleeding untreated; (d) A wait for the doctor loses the minutes that matter in a bleeding.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a look inside seems the careful FIRST step.

5-Second Recall: Garbhvati me khoon = andar ka jaanch nahi, turant hospital bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A bleeding late in pregnancy is moved to a centre with a vein line running.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A mother of a 6-day-old baby at home says that the cord stump is wet with a bad smell at the base. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Oil the stump with mustard oil and leave it as it is
option_2: Put a coin over the stump and tie the cord of the vest tight
option_3: Wash the stump with the water of the house and cover it with ash
option_4: Send the baby to the health centre at once and teach the mother the care of the stump
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Send the baby to the health centre at once and teach the mother the care of the stump

Clinical Rationale: A wet stump with a bad smell at the base is an infection of the cord, so the baby is sent to the centre at once and the mother is taught to keep the stump clean and dry.

Key Clue: 6-day-old baby with a wet cord stump and a bad smell at the base

Priority Principle: Newborn / Infection

Why Not Others: (a) Oil holds the damp and the smell against the stump; (b) A coin and a tight vest press the stump and hold the damp inside; (c) Unclean water and ash put more germs on the stump.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a wash seems the FIRST care of a dirty stump.

5-Second Recall: Naya bachcha aur gili-badbu wali naabhi = turant centre bhejo, saaf-sukha rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A stump that smells at the base is an infection and not simple dirt.

question: A young man of 30 years comes to the clinic with a cough for a month and a sputum report that shows the germ of tuberculosis. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the family to keep the man in a separate house
option_2: Give a syrup for the cough and ask the man to come after a month
option_3: Start the drugs of the programme for tuberculosis and note the family contacts
option_4: Send the man to the city hospital to start the treatment
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Start the drugs of the programme for tuberculosis and note the family contacts

Clinical Rationale: A report with the germ of tuberculosis is treated at once with the drugs of the national programme, and the family contacts are noted for testing.

Key Clue: young man of 30 years with a cough for a month and a report of the germ of tuberculosis

Priority Principle: Public health / Tuberculosis

Why Not Others: (a) A separate house does not take the place of treatment; (b) A syrup for the cough does not treat the germ of tuberculosis; (d) Treatment is started at the nearest centre and not sent on.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a city hospital seems the place for a serious disease.

5-Second Recall: TB ka germ report me = abhi dawa shuru, ghar walon ki jaanch.

PNC Exam Pearl: The treatment of tuberculosis is started at the nearest centre without a wait.

question: A 30-year-old woman who is receiving an injection of an antibiotic at the sub-centre has a puffed face, a tight chest and a fall in blood pressure within a minute. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a second dose of the antibiotic to complete the course
option_2: Stop the injection, give the drug for the reaction into the muscle and keep the vein open
option_3: Lay the woman flat with the legs down and give a sip of water
option_4: Note the reaction on the card and send the woman home in a car
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the injection, give the drug for the reaction into the muscle and keep the vein open

Clinical Rationale: A puffed face with a tight chest and a fall in blood pressure after an injection is a severe reaction, so the injection is stopped, the drug for the reaction is given and the vein is kept open at once.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman with a puffed face, a tight chest and a fall in blood pressure one minute after an injection

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Severe reaction

Why Not Others: (a) A second dose of the antibiotic deepens the reaction; (c) A sip of water is not safe in a woman with a tight chest; (d) Sending her home in a car leaves the reaction without care.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because lying flat seems the FIRST help in a faint.

5-Second Recall: Injection ke baad sooja chehra aur jakda seene = dawa roko, adrenaline, line kholo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The drug for a severe reaction is kept ready wherever an injection is given.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse of a sub-centre must carry the vaccine to a session of the village two hours away on a hot day, where a mother waits with her child for immunisation. Which action should the nurse take FIRST in the care of the vaccine?
option_1: Freeze the vaccine at the centre so that it stays cold on the way
option_2: Take the vaccine in the bag of the cycle and keep it in the shade at the site
option_3: Keep the vaccine in the cold box with the ice packs and check the vaccine vial monitor
option_4: Carry the vaccine in a flask with warm water to keep it from the heat
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the vaccine in the cold box with the ice packs and check the vaccine vial monitor

Clinical Rationale: The vaccine is carried in a cold box with the ice packs and the vial monitor is checked, so that the cold chain is NOT broken on the way to the village.

Key Clue: vaccine to be carried to a village session two hours away on a hot day

Priority Principle: Cold chain / Vaccine

Why Not Others: (a) A frozen vaccine loses its potency and is thrown away; (b) A shade at the site does not keep the vaccine cold on the way; (d) Warm water works against the cold chain of the vaccine.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the shade of a tree seems as cool as the shade.

5-Second Recall: Vaccine cold box me le jao, ice packs aur vial monitor check karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A vaccine that is frozen or warmed has lost its potency and is not used.

question: A nurse at a sub-centre has two vials of a vaccine open, and a woman waits with her 2-month-old child for the vaccine. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Send the children home and ask them to come the next day
option_2: Open both vials so that the children are NOT kept waiting
option_3: Keep the open vials for the next session of the week
option_4: Open one vial at a time and use it for all the children of the session
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Open one vial at a time and use it for all the children of the session

Clinical Rationale: One vial is opened at a time and used for the children of the session, because an open vial kept for a later day loses its potency.

Key Clue: two open vials of a vaccine for a small number of children at a session of the sub-centre

Priority Principle: Management / Vaccine

Why Not Others: (a) Children sent home may not come back for the vaccine; (b) Two open vials waste the vaccine that is left in them; (c) An open vial kept for days has lost its potency and is not used.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a short wait seems the wrong that must be stopped.

5-Second Recall: Ek time par ek hi vial kholo, bachche ka intezaar karwao mat.

PNC Exam Pearl: The open vial is used for the session and thrown away after it.

question: A community nurse visits the house of a 22-year-old woman who had a baby 10 days ago, and the family says the mother is NOT eating well because the baby is a girl. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Talk with the family about the care of the mother and the girl child and bring her to the centre
option_2: Advise the family to keep the mother in a separate room
option_3: Tell the mother to take only milk till the bleeding stops
option_4: Note the state of the mother in the register and visit after a month
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Talk with the family about the care of the mother and the girl child and bring her to the centre

Clinical Rationale: A mother who is NOT fed well after the birth is in danger of weakness and infection, so the nurse talks with the family and brings the mother to the centre at once.

Key Clue: 22-year-old woman 10 days after the birth who is NOT eating well because the baby is a girl

Priority Principle: Maternal care / Family

Why Not Others: (b) A separate room does not give the mother the food that she needs; (c) Milk alone does not give the strength that a mother needs after the birth; (d) A visit after a month lets the weakness grow in the mother.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because rest in a separate room seems the care of a mother.

5-Second Recall: Beti hone par maa ko khana nahi = parivar se baat karo, maa ko centre lao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The health of a mother after the birth is watched as the health of two lives.

question: A community nurse who visits the field is told of a 40-year-old man bitten on the foot by a snake about twenty minutes ago, and the foot is swollen with two fang marks. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Keep the man calm with the limb still and take him to the hospital at once
option_2: Tie a tight string above the bite and cut the wound with a blade
option_3: Ask the man to walk to the road so that the car comes faster
option_4: Put a hot pack on the foot and give a tablet for the pain
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the man calm with the limb still and take him to the hospital at once

Clinical Rationale: A bite with two fang marks and a swollen foot is treated by keeping the man calm with the limb still and taking him to the hospital at once, where the antivenom is given.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man bitten by a snake twenty minutes ago with a swollen foot and two fang marks

Priority Principle: Emergency / Snakebite

Why Not Others: (b) A tight string and a cut harm the limb and do not remove the venom; (c) A walk spreads the venom faster through the body; (d) A hot pack and a tablet for the pain do not treat the venom.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tight string above the bite seems the way to stop the venom.

5-Second Recall: Saap ka kaata = shaant rakho, ang still, turant hospital - katai ya rassi nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The limb is kept still and at the level of the heart on the way to the hospital.

question: A 40-year-old man is brought to the clinic with burns of the chest and arm from a kerosene stove, and the burnt skin is red with blisters. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the pain and ask the man to rest at home
option_2: Apply a paste of tooth powder to the burnt skin at once
option_3: Open the blisters with a needle to let the fluid out
option_4: Cool the burnt part with clean running water and cover it with a clean cloth
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Cool the burnt part with clean running water and cover it with a clean cloth

Clinical Rationale: Burns from a flame are cooled at once with clean running water and covered with a clean cloth, so that the heat is removed and the wound is kept clean.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man with burns of the chest and arm from a kerosene stove and red skin with blisters

Priority Principle: Emergency / Burns

Why Not Others: (a) Rest at home leaves the burns without the care that they need; (b) A paste on the burn holds the heat and brings infection; (c) An opened blister is a door for the germs of the centre.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the fluid of a blister seems the harm inside it.

5-Second Recall: Jalne par thanda behta paani - paste aur sui nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The cooling of a burn is started before the man is sent anywhere else.

question: A community nurse finds a 35-year-old man with a pale patch on the arm that has lost the sense of touch, and the man says a patch of this kind was treated in his father many years ago. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the man that the patch will go away with good food alone
option_2: Give an ointment for the patch and ask him to come after a month
option_3: Start the multi-drug treatment of the programme and examine the family of the man
option_4: Send the man to the city hospital for a test of the patch
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Start the multi-drug treatment of the programme and examine the family of the man

Clinical Rationale: A pale patch that has lost the sense of touch is a sign of leprosy, so the multi-drug treatment of the programme is started and the family is examined for other cases.

Key Clue: 35-year-old man with a pale patch on the arm that has lost the sense of touch and a father treated years ago

Priority Principle: Public health / Leprosy

Why Not Others: (a) Good food alone does not remove the germ; (b) An ointment alone does not treat the germ of leprosy; (d) Treatment is started at the nearest centre without delay.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because an ointment seems enough care for a patch of the skin.

5-Second Recall: Safed sookha dhabba jismein touch nahi = leprosy, MDT shuru, ghar dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The loss of the sense of touch is the sign that separates leprosy from other patches.

question: A 35-year-old man who attends the clinic and has taken the drugs of the programme for tuberculosis for five months brings a sputum report that still shows the germ. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the same drugs again for another three months and watch the man
option_2: Ask about the taking of the drugs and send the sputum for a drug-resistance test
option_3: Tell the man that the drugs of the programme have failed for him
option_4: Stop every drug and ask the man to come after a month for review
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Ask about the taking of the drugs and send the sputum for a drug-resistance test

Clinical Rationale: A sputum that still shows the germ after five months is examined for a fault in the taking of the drugs, and the sample is sent for a resistance test at once.

Key Clue: 35-year-old man on the drugs for tuberculosis for five months with a sputum that still shows the germ

Priority Principle: Public health / Drug resistance

Why Not Others: (a) The same drugs again do not treat a germ that has become resistant; (c) The word of a failure frightens the man away from treatment; (d) A stop of every drug lets the germ grow with no check.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the same drugs seem the safe longer course.

5-Second Recall: Paanch mahine baad bhi balgam me TB = dawa lene ka tareeka puchho, resistance test bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The adherence of the client is checked before the drugs are held to blame.

question: A community nurse visits the house of a 30-year-old woman who lost her husband a month ago and finds her sitting alone with a bottle of sleeping tablets in her hand. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Stay with the woman, take the tablets away and call the health team at once
option_2: Ask the woman to put the bottle away and come to the centre on her own
option_3: Tell the neighbours to watch the woman at night and go home
option_4: Note the state of the woman in the register and visit her after a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stay with the woman, take the tablets away and call the health team at once

Clinical Rationale: A woman who is sad after the loss of her husband and sits with a bottle of sleeping tablets is in danger, so the nurse stays with her, takes the tablets and calls the team at once.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman who lost her husband a month ago and sits with a bottle of sleeping tablets in her hand

Priority Principle: Safety / Mental health

Why Not Others: (b) Coming to the centre on her own leaves the woman alone with the tablets; (c) The neighbours are no guard against harm in the night; (d) A visit after a week is far too late for a danger of this kind.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a talk at the centre seems the answer for the sadness.

5-Second Recall: Ek maheene pehle pati ki maut aur haath me sleeping pills = saath raho, pills hato, team bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A loss with a bottle of tablets is read as a call for safety at once.

question: A 2-year-old child comes to the clinic with loose stools for two days, and the mother has already given the salt solution at home. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the worms along with the salt solution
option_2: Give a strong drug to stop the stools at once
option_3: Stop the salt solution because the stools have come down
option_4: Give zinc for fourteen days along with the salt solution for the stools
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Give zinc for fourteen days along with the salt solution for the stools

Clinical Rationale: Zinc is given for fourteen days along with the salt solution, because zinc brings down the number of days of the stools and the loss of water.

Key Clue: 2-year-old child with loose stools for two days who has taken the salt solution at home

Priority Principle: Child health / Loose stools

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet for the worms has no part in the treatment of the stools; (b) A strong drug to stop the stools holds the germ inside the bowel; (c) The salt solution is kept on till the stools stop.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a strong drug seems the fast stop of the stools.

5-Second Recall: Dast me ORS ke saath zinc 14 din - rokne wali dawa nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: Zinc shortens the loose stools and is given for a full fortnight.

question: A 30-year-old woman who attends the clinic has taken the drugs of the programme for tuberculosis for six weeks and now has yellow eyes and vomiting. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a strong drink of sugar cane juice to the woman
option_2: Continue the same drugs and give a syrup for the vomiting
option_3: Stop the drugs at once and send the woman to the doctor of the programme
option_4: Tell the woman that the yellow eyes will go with the treatment
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stop the drugs at once and send the woman to the doctor of the programme

Clinical Rationale: Yellow eyes with vomiting on the drugs for tuberculosis point to harm to the liver, so the drugs are stopped at once and the woman is sent to the doctor of the programme.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman on the drugs for tuberculosis for six weeks with yellow eyes and vomiting

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Harm to the liver

Why Not Others: (a) Sugar cane juice does not treat harm to the liver; (b) The same drugs go on harming the liver of the woman; (d) The yellow eyes are not part of the healing of the disease.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because the yellow colour seems a small part of the long treatment.

5-Second Recall: TB ki dawa se peeli aankhein = dawa turant band, programme doctor ko bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The drugs for tuberculosis are held at once when the liver shows harm.

question: A community nurse who visits the home finds that a mother has a packet of the salt solution meant for one litre of water and a bottle of 500 millilitres. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Mix the whole packet in the bottle so that the fluid is strong
option_2: Mix half of the packet in the full bottle of water and use it
option_3: Mix the whole packet and keep the rest of the fluid for the next day
option_4: Mix half of the packet in two bottles of water for later
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Mix half of the packet in the full bottle of water and use it

Clinical Rationale: The packet is meant for one litre, so half of the powder goes into the bottle of 500 millilitres and the fluid is used within a day.

Key Clue: packet of the salt solution for one litre and a bottle of 500 millilitres at the house of a child with stools

Priority Principle: Dehydration / Measure of the fluid

Why Not Others: (a) The whole packet in half of the water makes the fluid too strong; (c) Fluid kept for the next day is not safe to give; (d) Two bottles from the packet give a fluid of the wrong strength.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a strong fluid seems the faster repair.

5-Second Recall: Ek packet ek litre ka - aadhe litre me aadha packet, aur wo bhi ek din ke andar.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fluid that is stronger than the measure harms the child.

question: A community nurse must visit four houses in a village this morning, and one house has a mother whose 5-day-old baby has a wet and smelly cord stump. Which house should the nurse visit FIRST?
option_1: The house with the woman who is four months pregnant
option_2: The house with the 5-day-old baby and the wet and smelly cord stump
option_3: The house with the old man who takes a drug for the pressure
option_4: The house with the child who is to be weighed this month
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The house with the 5-day-old baby and the wet and smelly cord stump

Clinical Rationale: A 5-day-old baby with a wet and smelly cord stump can get a dangerous infection, so this house is visited before the others in the village.

Key Clue: four houses of a village and one with a 5-day-old baby with a wet and smelly cord stump

Priority Principle: Home visits / Priority

Why Not Others: (a) The routine check of a pregnancy can wait for the next visit; (c) The man on a drug for the pressure is seen on a fixed day; (d) The monthly weighing of a child is done at the centre.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a pregnancy seems the visit that the nurse should NOT miss.

5-Second Recall: Ghar ke visit me pehle naya bachcha jiski naabhi gili-badbu wali hai.

PNC Exam Pearl: Home visits are ordered by the danger to the client and not by the list.

question: A community nurse visits the school and finds that the children who attend the school, including a child of 8 years, pass stool in the open field because it has no toilet. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the school and the village to build toilets and teach the children to use them
option_2: Give a tablet for the worms to all the children of the school
option_3: Ask the children to go home for the stool during school hours
option_4: Note the state of the school and report to the officer after a month
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Tell the school and the village to build toilets and teach the children to use them

Clinical Rationale: Stool passed in the open carries germs to the food and the water, so the school and the village are told to build toilets and the children are taught to use them.

Key Clue: children of a village school who pass stool in the open field because the school has no toilet

Priority Principle: Public health / Sanitation

Why Not Others: (b) A tablet for the worms does not stop the passing of stool in the open; (c) A walk home for every stool takes the children out of the class; (d) A report after a month lets the practice go on in the school.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tablet for the worms seems the clean end of the problem.

5-Second Recall: Khule me shauch = school me toilet banao, bachchon ko istemaal sikhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A toilet that is built and not used does not help the health of the village.

question: A 22-year-old woman brings her 15-month-old child to the clinic and says the child takes only breast milk and no other food. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Give only fruit juice till the child takes food well
option_2: Stop breast milk so that the child takes food
option_3: Give the child buffalo milk in a bottle
option_4: Start the child on soft food of the family along with breast milk
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Start the child on soft food of the family along with breast milk

Clinical Rationale: A 15-month-old child needs soft food of the family along with breast milk, because milk alone does NOT give the energy and iron that the child needs.

Key Clue: 15-month-old child who takes only breast milk and no other food

Priority Principle: Nutrition / Feeding of the child

Why Not Others: (a) Fruit juice alone does not give the child energy for growth; (b) Stopping breast milk takes away a food of value; (c) A bottle of buffalo milk brings infection and no iron.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because fruit juice seems the soft food for a small child.

5-Second Recall: 15 mahine ka bachcha sirf doodh par = parivar ka naram khana shuru karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Food of the family is started in small soft amounts along with the breast feeds.

question: A nurse of a sub-centre is about to give a vaccine to a child who comes to the clinic and sees that the square on the vaccine vial monitor is as dark as the outer circle. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Use the vial after shaking it well for a minute
option_2: Use the vial at once because the vaccine is still cold
option_3: Keep the vial aside and throw it away without using the vaccine
option_4: Put the vial in the cold box for the next session of the week
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the vial aside and throw it away without using the vaccine

Clinical Rationale: A square that has become as dark as the outer circle shows that the vaccine has taken heat, so the vial is thrown away and is NOT used.

Key Clue: a vial of vaccine whose square on the monitor has become as dark as the outer circle

Priority Principle: Cold chain / Vaccine

Why Not Others: (a) Shaking does not bring back the potency of a spoiled vaccine; (b) A vaccine that has taken heat has lost its potency and does not protect; (d) A spoiled vial in the cold box spoils the other vials.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a cold vial seems a safe vial.

5-Second Recall: VVM ka square gehra = vaccine kharab, phenko - istemaal mat karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The monitor on the vial is read before the vaccine is drawn.

question: A 40-year-old man who takes lithium is brought to the clinic with a level of 1.9 mEq/L, vomiting and a coarse tremor of the hands. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a syrup for the vomiting and ask the man to rest
option_2: Give the next dose of the drug and note the tremor in the chart
option_3: Hold the drug, give the salt solution and inform the doctor at once
option_4: Send the man home and take the level of the drug after a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Hold the drug, give the salt solution and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A level of 1.9 mEq/L with vomiting and a coarse tremor is too high, so the drug is held, the salt solution is given and the doctor is told at once.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man on lithium with a level of 1.9 mEq/L, vomiting and a coarse tremor

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Drug level

Why Not Others: (a) A syrup for the vomiting leaves the level of the drug high; (b) More of the drug takes the level higher and the harm deeper; (d) A wait of a week with a high level harms the man.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the ordered dose seems the plain duty of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Lithium level 1.9 aur kampan-ulti = dawa roko, doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Vomiting with a tremor on lithium points to a level that is too high.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A 30-year-old man comes to the clinic with a white patch inside the mouth that does NOT come away, and he chews tobacco with lime the whole day. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet of vitamins for a month and ask him to come again
option_2: Send the man to the health centre for a look at the patch and talk about the tobacco
option_3: Tell the man to wash the mouth with salt water every day
option_4: Note the patch in the register and look at it after three months
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Send the man to the health centre for a look at the patch and talk about the tobacco

Clinical Rationale: A white patch in the mouth of a man who chews tobacco may turn into cancer, so the man is sent for a look at the patch and is talked to about the tobacco at once.

Key Clue: 30-year-old man with a white patch in the mouth that does NOT come away and a habit of chewing tobacco with lime

Priority Principle: Public health / Tobacco

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet of vitamins does not take away the patch of the mouth; (c) A wash of salt water does not treat a patch of this kind; (d) A look after three months lets the patch change in the mouth.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a vitamin seems the simple care of a patch of the mouth.

5-Second Recall: Muh me safed dhabba aur tambaku = turant centre bhejo, tambaku chhudwao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A white patch that does not come away is examined before it is treated.

question: A 50-year-old man of the village comes to the clinic with a pressure of 180/110 mmHg a month after he stopped the drug for blood pressure because he felt well. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Restart the drug on the order of the doctor and teach the man why it is taken daily
option_2: Tell the man that he may take the drug only on the days of the headache
option_3: Ask the man to stop the salt and to come again after a month
option_4: Give a strong drug of the pressure at once and send the man home
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Restart the drug on the order of the doctor and teach the man why it is taken daily

Clinical Rationale: A pressure of 180/110 mmHg after a month without the drug is treated by restarting the drug on the order of the doctor and by teaching the man that it is taken daily for life.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man who stopped the drug for blood pressure a month ago and now reads 180/110 mmHg

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Long treatment

Why Not Others: (b) A drug taken only with the headache leaves the pressure high on other days; (c) Less salt helps the pressure but does not take the place of the drug; (d) A strong drug without an order and without a check is not given by the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because less salt seems the whole care of a high pressure.

5-Second Recall: BP 180/110 aur dawa band = dawa wapas shuru, roz lene ka kaaran samjhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A pressure drug is taken every day and not on the days of a complaint.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse is to make the FIRST home visit to a family with a 4-day-old newborn in a village. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Teach the mother the care of the breast and the feeding
option_2: Weigh the baby and note the weight on the card
option_3: Look at the cord stump of the baby and dress it
option_4: Wash the hands and ask the family about the baby and the mother
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Wash the hands and ask the family about the baby and the mother

Clinical Rationale: The nurse washes the hands and asks the family about the baby and the mother, so that the state of both is known before any care is given.

Key Clue: FIRST home visit to a family with a 4-day-old newborn in a village

Priority Principle: Home visit / Procedure

Why Not Others: (a) Teaching the feeding comes after the state of the baby is known; (b) Weighing comes after the talk with the family and the look at the baby; (c) The cord stump is looked at after the hands are washed.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the weight seems the FIRST work of the visit.

5-Second Recall: Ghar ke pehle visit me: haath dhoyo, phir maa-bachche ki baat aur dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A home visit begins with clean hands and the talk with the family.

question: A community nurse who visits the village finds from the records that six children below 5 years died in the year, four of them with loose stools, and the mother of one of them asks why. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the salt solution to every house of the village at once
option_2: Report the six deaths to the officer and wait for orders
option_3: Advise the families of the dead children to keep the houses clean
option_4: Work out the causes of the deaths and make a plan against the loose stools
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Work out the causes of the deaths and make a plan against the loose stools

Clinical Rationale: Four deaths of small children from loose stools in a year show a fault that can be set right, so the causes are worked out and a plan against the loose stools is made.

Key Clue: six deaths of children below 5 years in a year in a village, four of them with loose stools

Priority Principle: Public health / Deaths of children

Why Not Others: (a) A bag of the salt solution for every house is no plan against the cause; (b) A report with a wait leaves the cause of the deaths untouched; (c) A word to the homes of the dead children does not stop new deaths.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the salt solution seems the answer to the loose stools.

5-Second Recall: Bachchon ki maut ka data dekho, kaaran dhoondo, phir plan banao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The deaths of children are counted and the cause behind them is looked for.

question: A nurse is to dress the wound of a client in the house, and the room is dark with the bed covered by the clothes of the family. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the family to put on the light of the room and work on the bed
option_2: Dress the wound on the bed with the light of the door of the room
option_3: Ask the family to clear a table in good light and lay the packet of the dressing on it
option_4: Take the client to the door of the house and dress the wound there
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Ask the family to clear a table in good light and lay the packet of the dressing on it

Clinical Rationale: A clean place in good light is made ready before the packet is opened, so that the wound is seen and the dressing is kept free of the germs of the room.

Key Clue: a wound to be dressed in a dark house with a bed covered by the clothes of the family

Priority Principle: Procedure / Wound care at home

Why Not Others: (a) The light alone does not give the clean place that the dressing needs; (b) A dressing on a covered bed is done in the dark and among the clothes; (d) The door of the house is no place for the dressing of a wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the light seems the whole need of a dressing.

5-Second Recall: Ghar me dressing se pehle saaf jagah aur achhi roshni banao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The packet of the dressing is opened only on a clean and lit surface.

question: A house in a village has had a case of a disease that spreads by air, and the nurse is to make the house safe for the family after the client is taken to the hospital. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Burn the clothes and the bedding of the client in the yard at once
option_2: Air the rooms in the open sun and wash the floor and the walls with a disinfectant
option_3: Close the doors and the windows of the house for two days
option_4: Wash the rooms with the plain water of the pump and dry them
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Air the rooms in the open sun and wash the floor and the walls with a disinfectant

Clinical Rationale: A house of a disease that spreads by air is made safe by the sun and the air with a wash of the floor and the walls with a disinfectant.

Key Clue: a house of a case of a disease that spreads by air after the client was taken to the hospital

Priority Principle: Infection control / House of a case

Why Not Others: (a) A burn of the clothes wastes the goods of a poor family; (c) A closed house holds the germs inside its rooms; (d) Plain water does not take the germs off the walls and the floor.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a fire in the yard seems the surest way to kill the germs.

5-Second Recall: Hawa se failne wali bimari ke ghar ko dhoop-hawa aur disinfectant se saaf karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The sun and the air with a disinfectant wash are the simple end of the germs of a house.

question: A 30-year-old man comes to the clinic with a deep cut on the foot with mud inside it after walking in the wet field without shoes. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Clean the wound and take the vaccine against tetanus at the centre at once
option_2: Wash the foot with the water of the field and cover it with a cloth
option_3: Put the leaf of a plant on the wound and tie it with a thread
option_4: Wait for three days and take the vaccine if the foot swells
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the wound and take the vaccine against tetanus at the centre at once

Clinical Rationale: A deep cut with mud of the field is a wound that takes the germ of tetanus, so the wound is cleaned and the vaccine is taken at once.

Key Clue: 30-year-old man with a deep cut on the foot with mud inside after walking in the wet field without shoes

Priority Principle: Public health / Tetanus

Why Not Others: (b) A cloth over the wound holds the mud and the germs inside; (c) A leaf and a thread keep the wound dirty and closed; (d) A wait of three days lets the germ of tetanus settle in the wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a leaf on the wound seems the care of the village.

5-Second Recall: Mitti wala gehra ghaav = saaf karo aur tetanus ka vaccine turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: A dirty deep cut takes the vaccine at once and not after the swelling.

question: A community nurse is to weigh a 1-year-old child who has come to the anganwadi with his mother. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put the child on the scale with the clothes and the shoes on
option_2: Note the name and the age of the child and set the scale to the zero mark
option_3: Ask the mother to hold the child on the scale with her
option_4: Weigh the child after the morning feed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Note the name and the age of the child and set the scale to the zero mark

Clinical Rationale: The name and the age are noted and the scale is set to the zero mark before the child is put on it, so that the weight is correct and is entered on the card.

Key Clue: a 1-year-old child to be weighed at the anganwadi

Priority Principle: Procedure / Weight of the child

Why Not Others: (a) Clothes and shoes add to the weight of the small child; (c) A weight taken with the mother is not the weight of the child; (d) A feed before the weight makes the reading wrong.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the clothes of the child seem part of the child.

5-Second Recall: Wazan se pehle naam-umar note karo aur scale zero par lao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A scale that is not set to zero gives a weight that misleads.

question: A 3-year-old child has had a fever with a rash of red spots behind the ears and on the face for three days, and now the mother says the eyes are red with a discharge. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the mother that the rash will go away with the fever
option_2: Give a syrup for the fever and ask the mother to come after a week
option_3: Give vitamin A at once and look at the eyes of the child in good light
option_4: Wash the eyes with the water of the house and cover them with a cloth
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Give vitamin A at once and look at the eyes of the child in good light

Clinical Rationale: A fever with a rash behind the ears and red eyes points to measles, so vitamin A is given at once and the eyes are examined in good light, because the eyes may lose their sight.

Key Clue: 3-year-old child with fever, a rash of red spots behind the ears and red eyes with a discharge

Priority Principle: Child health / Measles

Why Not Others: (a) The rash is not the whole illness of a child with measles; (b) A syrup for the fever leaves the eyes and the vitamin A without care; (d) A cloth over the eye holds the discharge inside.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the rash seems the whole illness of the child.

5-Second Recall: Khasra me vitamin A turant, aur aankhon ki jaanch tez roshni me.

PNC Exam Pearl: Vitamin A is given in measles to save the eyes and to bring the illness down.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse who visits the field finds a 55-year-old man with a heavy pain in the chest that goes to the left arm, and he is sweating with cold skin. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give him a drink of cold water and rub the chest with oil
option_2: Give a tablet for the pain and let him rest in the shade of a tree
option_3: Ask him to walk slowly to the road and wait for a bus there
option_4: Stop the work, sit him up and send him to the hospital at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Stop the work, sit him up and send him to the hospital at once

Clinical Rationale: A heavy pain in the chest that goes to the left arm with sweating points to a heart attack, so the work is stopped, the man is sat up and he is sent to the hospital at once.

Key Clue: 55-year-old man with a heavy pain in the chest that goes to the left arm and sweating with cold skin

Priority Principle: ABC / Heart attack

Why Not Others: (a) A rub of oil and cold water do not treat a heart attack; (b) A tablet for the pain and rest in the shade waste the first minutes; (c) A walk to the road takes the heart further away from help.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a walk to the road seems the way to the hospital.

5-Second Recall: Seene me bhaari dard aur thanda paseena = kaam roko, baithao, turant hospital.

PNC Exam Pearl: A pain of the chest that goes to the arm is a heart attack till it is proved otherwise.

question: A mother brings her 4-month-old child to the clinic and says the child vomits the milk after every feed and has NOT gained weight since birth. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Look at the way the child is fed and weigh the child at once
option_2: Give a drug to stop the vomiting and send the child home
option_3: Tell the mother that vomiting in a baby is always normal
option_4: Change the milk of the child to the milk of a tin at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Look at the way the child is fed and weigh the child at once

Clinical Rationale: A 4-month-old child who vomits every feed and has NOT gained weight is watched while feeding and is weighed at once, because the fault may lie in the way of feeding.

Key Clue: 4-month-old child who vomits the milk after every feed and has NOT gained weight since birth

Priority Principle: Child health / Feeding

Why Not Others: (b) A drug to stop the vomiting hides the cause of the trouble; (c) A weight that does not rise is not a normal part of the growing of a baby; (d) A tin of milk before the feed is seen wastes the milk of the mother.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because vomiting in a baby seems a small matter of the age.

5-Second Recall: Char mahine ka bachcha doodh ugalta hai aur wazan nahi badha = feed dekh kar pilao, wazan lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A child who does not gain weight is watched while feeding before any drug.

question: A 60-year-old woman at home takes a tablet that thins the blood, and the family says that she took a second tablet by mistake three hours ago. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the double dose on the card and visit the house after two days
option_2: Give a tablet of the same drug at the usual hour of the night
option_3: Give a glass of milk and ask the woman to lie down
option_4: Inform the doctor at once and look for bleeding from the gums and the skin
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Inform the doctor at once and look for bleeding from the gums and the skin

Clinical Rationale: A double dose of a drug that thins the blood is reported to the doctor at once, and the woman is examined for bleeding from the gums and the skin.

Key Clue: 60-year-old woman who took a second tablet of a drug that thins the blood three hours ago

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Double dose

Why Not Others: (a) A visit after two days misses the hours when bleeding may start; (b) The usual dose on the night of a double dose adds to the danger; (c) Milk and rest do not change the state of the blood.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because milk seems the simple guard against a strong drug.

5-Second Recall: Khoon patla karne wali dawa do guna = doctor ko batao, khoon ke nishaan dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: A double dose of a blood-thinning drug is watched for bleeding on the same day.

question: A mother brings her 1-year-old child to the sub-centre, and the nurse notes a dry eye with a small patch on the white of the eye. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give vitamin A at once on the order and send the child to the hospital
option_2: Give a syrup of vitamins and ask the mother to come after a month
option_3: Wash the eye with salt water and put a pad on it
option_4: Tell the mother that the eye will become clean with good food
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give vitamin A at once on the order and send the child to the hospital

Clinical Rationale: A dry eye with a patch on the white of the eye is harm to the eye from a lack of vitamin A, so the vitamin is given at once and the child is sent to the hospital.

Key Clue: 1-year-old child with a dry eye and a small patch on the white of the eye

Priority Principle: Child health / Lack of vitamin A

Why Not Others: (b) A syrup for a month is far too slow for an eye that is harmed; (c) A wash and a pad do not treat the lack of the vitamin; (d) Good food alone does not bring back an eye that has lost its power.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because good food seems the whole cure of a weak child.

5-Second Recall: Sookhi aankh aur safed dhabba = vitamin A abhi do, hospital bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The eyes of a child with measles or poor food are examined before the sight is lost.

question: A 45-year-old man is brought to the clinic after a fall from a bicycle with a bent forearm, and the hand below the bend is pale and has no pulse. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Pull the bent forearm straight to set the bone
option_2: Keep the arm still as it lies and send the man to the hospital at once
option_3: Put a tight cloth round the arm and tie the hand to the chest
option_4: Give a tablet for the pain and ask the man to come after a day
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Keep the arm still as it lies and send the man to the hospital at once

Clinical Rationale: A bend of the forearm with a pale hand and no pulse is an injury of the vessel, so the arm is kept still as it lies and the man is sent to the hospital at once.

Key Clue: 45-year-old man with a bent forearm after a fall and a hand below the bend that is pale with no pulse

Priority Principle: Emergency / Bone and vessel

Why Not Others: (a) A pull on the bent bone can harm the vessel and the nerves of the arm; (c) A tight cloth round the arm stops the flow of blood in a limb that is short of it; (d) A wait of a day can cost the man his hand.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because setting the bone seems the FIRST help for a broken arm.

5-Second Recall: Toota haath, safed haath, pulse nahi = hilao mat, turant hospital.

PNC Exam Pearl: A limb that is pale and without a pulse is a limb in danger of being lost.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 65-year-old man at home who has taken only thin rice water for many days after a fever now has sunken eyes and cannot get up from the bed, and the family asks what to give him. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give only coconut water for the day
option_2: Give a large feed of rice and pulse at once to fill the weakness
option_3: Start feeds in small amounts often and send the man to the health centre
option_4: Tell the family to give the man tea with sugar many times a day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Start feeds in small amounts often and send the man to the health centre

Clinical Rationale: A man who is very weak after many days of thin rice water is started on feeds in small amounts often, and he is sent to the health centre for full care.

Key Clue: 65-year-old man who took only thin rice water for many days after a fever and now has sunken eyes and cannot get up

Priority Principle: Nutrition / Slow repair

Why Not Others: (a) Coconut water gives no protein for the repair of the body; (b) A large feed in one sitting cannot be taken by a weak man; (d) Tea with sugar gives energy but no protein for the repair.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a large feed seems the fast way to fill the weakness.

5-Second Recall: Kamzor client ko thoda-thoda khaana baar-baar, ek saath nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The feeding of a very weak client is started in small amounts and watched.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse visits the village where a mother tells her of many cases of loose stools, and the nurse must find the cause of the illness. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Send the stool samples of a few persons to the laboratory
option_2: Give the salt solution to the persons who are ill in the houses
option_3: Write the signs that make a case and find all the persons who fit them
option_4: Chlorinate the water of the wells of the village
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Write the signs that make a case and find all the persons who fit them

Clinical Rationale: The signs that make a case are written and every person who fits them is found, so that the number and the spread of the illness are known before the cause is looked for.

Key Clue: many cases of loose stools in a village whose cause is to be found

Priority Principle: Public health / Look for the cause

Why Not Others: (a) Samples before the cases are counted may be taken from the wrong persons; (b) The salt solution treats the ill persons but does not find the cause; (d) Chlorination before the cause is known wastes the work of the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the laboratory report seems the FIRST need of a search for a cause.

5-Second Recall: Outbreak me pehle case definition banao, saare case dhoondo, phir kaaran.

PNC Exam Pearl: A case definition is written before the cases of an outbreak are counted.

question: A 25-year-old woman who attends the sub-centre with a high fever must be sent to the district hospital. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the case in the register and wait for the ambulance
option_2: Give a tablet for the fever and put the woman in the car of the village
option_3: Ask the family to take the woman and to tell the doctor about her
option_4: Write a note with the signs, the care given and the hour, and send it with the woman
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Write a note with the signs, the care given and the hour, and send it with the woman

Clinical Rationale: A note with the signs, the care given and the hour is written and sent with the woman, so that the hospital begins the care where the centre left it.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman with a high fever to be sent to the district hospital from the sub-centre

Priority Principle: Procedure / Referral

Why Not Others: (a) A wait for the ambulance of the district leaves the woman without care; (b) A tablet for the fever is given, but a woman sent without a note loses her story; (c) The family cannot tell the signs that the nurse has taken.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the family seems the people who know the illness.

5-Second Recall: Refer karte waqt likhi hui parchi bhejo - signs, dawa, samay.

PNC Exam Pearl: A referral is not complete without the note that carries the findings.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 50-year-old man at home has a wound on the leg with redness that spreads up the leg, and the skin is hot with a temperature of 39 degrees Celsius, and the family asks the nurse to see him. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Keep the leg raised and send the man to the hospital at once
option_2: Put a warm pack on the red skin and dress the wound again
option_3: Give a tablet for the fever and ask the man to rest at home
option_4: Wash the wound with soap and tie a cloth over it
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the leg raised and send the man to the hospital at once

Clinical Rationale: Redness that spreads up the leg with heat and fever is an infection of the flesh, so the leg is raised and the man is sent to the hospital at once.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man with a wound on the leg, redness that spreads up the leg, hot skin and a temperature of 39

Priority Principle: Infection / Spreading redness

Why Not Others: (b) A warm pack over the redness spreads the infection faster; (c) A tablet for the fever and rest at home leave the infection growing; (d) A cloth over the wound holds the infection inside the leg.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a warm pack seems the relief of a painful leg.

5-Second Recall: Ghaav se laali oopar tak aur bukhar = paon uncha karo, turant hospital.

PNC Exam Pearl: A redness that moves up a limb in hours is treated as an emergency of the flesh.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 25-year-old woman who attends the sub-centre in the seventh month of pregnancy says she has had no injection against tetanus in this pregnancy. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the woman that the vaccine is NOT given after the sixth month
option_2: Give the vaccine of the schedule today and note it on the card of the mother
option_3: Ask the woman to come after the birth for the vaccine
option_4: Give only the iron and calcium tablets and note the visit
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give the vaccine of the schedule today and note it on the card of the mother

Clinical Rationale: The vaccine against tetanus is given in the schedule of the pregnancy even in the seventh month, and it is noted on the card of the mother.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman in the seventh month of pregnancy with no injection against tetanus in this pregnancy

Priority Principle: Health promotion / Immunisation of the mother

Why Not Others: (a) The vaccine is given at any month of the pregnancy and not before a set month; (c) A vaccine after the birth does not guard the mother and the baby during the birth; (d) The iron tablets do not take the place of the vaccine against tetanus.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the birth seems the hour when the needle is needed.

5-Second Recall: Garbhvati ko TT ka teeka schedule ke hisaab se - mahine ka intezaar nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The guard against tetanus is built before the birth and not after it.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A 30-year-old woman comes to the clinic with a weight of 42 kg, a height of 1.5 metres and a haemoglobin of 9 g/dL. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the low weight and start iron tablets with advice on food of good value
option_2: Tell the woman that her weight is right for her height
option_3: Give a tablet to bring down the weight of the woman
option_4: Ask the woman to rest at home and to take less food
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Note the low weight and start iron tablets with advice on food of good value

Clinical Rationale: A weight of 42 kg with a height of 1.5 metres gives a body mass index below 18.5, so the low weight is noted and iron tablets with advice on food are started.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman with a weight of 42 kg, a height of 1.5 metres and haemoglobin 9 g/dL

Priority Principle: Nutrition / Weight for height

Why Not Others: (b) The weight for this height is below the healthy range; (c) A tablet to bring the weight down harms a woman who is already thin; (d) Less food takes the weight and the blood lower still.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the numbers seem a weight that is right.

5-Second Recall: Wazan 42 kg aur height 1.5 m = BMI kam, iron aur poshan shuru karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The weight is read with the height before any advice on food is given.

question: A 60-year-old man comes to the clinic with a swelling in the groin that appears on standing and goes back on lying down, and he lifts heavy loads the whole day. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the pain and ask him to come after a month
option_2: Tell the man that the swelling will go away with a tight band
option_3: Ask the man to press the swelling back inside with the hand
option_4: Tell the man to stop lifting loads and to come for repair of the swelling
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Tell the man to stop lifting loads and to come for repair of the swelling

Clinical Rationale: A swelling of the groin that appears on standing is a break of the wall of the abdomen, so heavy lifting is stopped and the man is sent for repair of the swelling.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man with a swelling in the groin that appears on standing and goes back on lying down and a day of lifting loads

Priority Principle: Surgery / Break of the abdominal wall

Why Not Others: (a) A wait of a month lets the swelling grow larger with the lifting; (b) A tight band does not close the break in the wall of the abdomen; (c) Pressing the swelling back can catch the bowel inside it.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tight band seems the easy answer for a swelling.

5-Second Recall: Khade hone par groin me soojan = bhaar uthana band, operation ke liye bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A swelling that appears on standing is repaired before the bowel is caught in it.

question: A 75-year-old man at home who walks with a stick gets up at night for the toilet, and the house has no light on the way and the family asks how to keep him safe. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the old man to walk less at night and to drink less water
option_2: Ask the family to keep the old man in bed for the whole night
option_3: Arrange a light on the way and a pan near the bed for the night
option_4: Give a tablet to make him sleep so that he gets up less often
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Arrange a light on the way and a pan near the bed for the night
