Clinical Rationale: A dark way to the toilet at night is the common cause of a fall at home, so a light is arranged on the way and a pan is kept near the bed.

Key Clue: 75-year-old man who walks with a stick, gets up for the toilet at night and has no light on the way

Priority Principle: Safety / Fall at home

Why Not Others: (a) Less water at night does not take away the dark way to the toilet; (b) Keeping the man in bed does not stop the need to pass urine; (d) A tablet for sleep makes a fall at night more likely.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a good sleep seems the safe night for an old man.

5-Second Recall: Raat me andhere me toilet jaana = light lagao, paas me pan rakho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The dangers of the house are set right before the old man is told to be careful.

question: A community nurse who visits the school finds a 6-year-old child with a rash of small blisters on the chest and the back, and the child has a slight fever. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the fever and let the child sit in the class
option_2: Send the child home and look at the other children of the class for the same rash
option_3: Put a powder on the rash and ask the child to keep the shirt on
option_4: Note the rash in the register and tell the teacher to watch the child
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Send the child home and look at the other children of the class for the same rash

Clinical Rationale: A rash of small blisters with a mild fever in a school child spreads from child to child, so the child is sent home and the others in the class are examined.

Key Clue: 6-year-old child in a school with a rash of small blisters on the chest and the back and a slight fever

Priority Principle: School health / Rash

Why Not Others: (a) A child with a rash that spreads stays out of the class; (c) A powder and a shirt over the rash do not stop the spread of the illness; (d) A word to the teacher is no guard for the other children.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a mild fever seems a small matter of the class.

5-Second Recall: Blister wale daane aur halka bukhar = bachche ko ghar bhejo aur class dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: In a school the class is examined and not only the ill child.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 25-year-old woman who is 8 weeks pregnant comes to the clinic with slight bleeding from the birth passage and a mild pain in the lower abdomen. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the woman to do the work of the house as before and watch
option_2: Tell the woman that slight bleeding is common in early pregnancy
option_3: Give a drug to stop the bleeding and send her home at once
option_4: Send the woman for a look at the pregnancy and tell her to rest
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Send the woman for a look at the pregnancy and tell her to rest

Clinical Rationale: Bleeding in the early months of pregnancy is sent for a look at the pregnancy and the woman is told to rest, so that the state of the pregnancy is known.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman, 8 weeks pregnant, with slight bleeding from the birth passage and mild pain in the lower abdomen

Priority Principle: Early pregnancy / Bleeding

Why Not Others: (a) The work of the house as before brings more bleeding; (b) Slight bleeding is not waved away without a look at the pregnancy; (c) A drug to stop the bleeding without a look hides the state of the pregnancy.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a slight bleed seems a common part of early pregnancy.

5-Second Recall: Shuru ke mahine me khoon = jaanch ke liye bhejo, aaraam karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every bleeding in pregnancy is examined before it is called common.

question: A nurse in a village camp is to collect a drop of blood from the finger of a man who attends the camp. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the hands, wear gloves and take a fresh lancet from the packet
option_2: Clean the finger of the man with spirit and prick it
option_3: Take the drop of blood on the slide and write the name after it
option_4: Put the used lancet in the bin of the camp and note the case
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the hands, wear gloves and take a fresh lancet from the packet

Clinical Rationale: The hands are cleaned and gloves are worn and a fresh lancet is taken before the finger is pricked, so that the nurse and the client are both safe.

Key Clue: a drop of blood to be collected from the finger of an adult in a village camp

Priority Principle: Procedure / Blood sample

Why Not Others: (b) The finger is cleaned after the gloves and the fresh lancet are ready; (c) The name is written on the slide before the drop is taken; (d) The lancet is thrown away after the drop is taken, not as the first step.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the clean finger seems the FIRST need of the test.

5-Second Recall: Finger prick se pehle haath dhoyo, gloves pehno, nayi lancet lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fresh lancet for every person is the rule of every camp.

question: A community nurse who visits the village is told by a mother that many persons get malaria every year in the weeks after the rains. Which action should the nurse take FIRST before the season comes?
option_1: Wait for the FIRST cases and treat them with the drugs of the programme
option_2: Make a plan against the mosquito in the village before the rains begin
option_3: Give the drug for malaria to every person of the village before the rains
option_4: Ask the families to keep the windows of the houses closed at night
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Make a plan against the mosquito in the village before the rains begin

Clinical Rationale: Cases that come every year with the rains are stopped by a plan against the mosquito in the village before the season, and NOT by a drug for every person.

Key Clue: village with many cases of malaria every year in the weeks after the rains

Priority Principle: Public health / Plan before the season

Why Not Others: (a) A wait for the first cases lets the illness settle in the village; (c) A drug for every person is no guard for a whole season; (d) Closed windows do not remove the water in which the mosquito breeds.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a drug for all seems the sure guard of the village.

5-Second Recall: Har saal baarish ke baad malaria = season se pehle plan banao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The work against a disease of the season is done before the season.

question: A family in a village with a 22-year-old woman in the eighth month of pregnancy has no money for the birth in hospital. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Advise the family to have the birth at home with the help of a neighbour
option_2: Ask the family to arrange the money from the village at once
option_3: Tell the family about the government scheme for a birth in hospital and help with the papers
option_4: Note the case in the register and visit the house after the birth
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Tell the family about the government scheme for a birth in hospital and help with the papers

Clinical Rationale: A family that cannot pay for the birth of a baby is told about the government scheme for a birth in hospital and is helped with the papers, so that the birth is safe.

Key Clue: family of a village with a woman of 22 years in the eighth month of pregnancy and no money for a hospital birth

Priority Principle: Safe birth / Help of the scheme

Why Not Others: (a) A birth at home with a neighbour is a risk that the scheme can avert; (b) Money raised from the village is not the duty of a poor family; (d) A visit after the birth is far too late for a safe birth.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a neighbour at the birth seems the help of the village.

5-Second Recall: Hospital ke paise nahi = sarkari yojana batao, kaagaz me madad karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Money is never the reason for a birth at home in a village of the scheme.

question: A community nurse who visits the field finds a 40-year-old man who works in the summer heat fallen down with hot and dry skin and a temperature of 41 degrees Celsius, and he is NOT awake. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the man to the house of the family and wait for the doctor
option_2: Give a drink of cold water by mouth to the man
option_3: Cover the man with a wet sheet and give a tablet for the fever
option_4: Move the man to the shade and bring the heat of the body down at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Move the man to the shade and bring the heat of the body down at once

Clinical Rationale: Hot and dry skin with a temperature of 41 and a man who is NOT awake is a heat stroke, so he is moved to the shade and the heat of the body is brought down at once.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man who works in the summer field and falls with hot dry skin, a temperature of 41 and no waking

Priority Principle: ABC / Heat stroke

Why Not Others: (a) A wait for the doctor in a house loses the minutes that matter; (b) A drink by mouth in a man who is not awake can enter the lungs; (c) A wet sheet with a wait does not bring the temperature down fast enough.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a cold drink seems the whole answer for a hot body.

5-Second Recall: Garmi me behosh aur sookhi garam chamdi = chhaya me le jao, turant thanda karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The body is cooled in a heat stroke even before the man is moved far.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse at a sub-centre must decide the rate that is too fast for a 4-month-old child whose mother has brought him with a cough, and the chart of the counting of the breathing hangs on the wall. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Count the breathing of the child for one full minute and read the cut-off for the age
option_2: Take the rate of the child for fifteen seconds and multiply it by four
option_3: Judge the rate by the look of the chest of the child
option_4: Use the cut-off of an older child for all the children of the centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Count the breathing of the child for one full minute and read the cut-off for the age

Clinical Rationale: The breathing is counted for one full minute and the cut-off for the age group is read on the chart, because a 4-month-old child breathes faster than an older child when well and ill.

Key Clue: the chart of the counting of the breathing on the wall and a child of 4 months with a cough

Priority Principle: Child health / Count of the breathing

Why Not Others: (b) A count of fifteen seconds multiplied misses the small changes of breathing; (c) A look at the chest alone does not give the rate that decides the care; (d) The cut-off changes with the age of the child and is not the same for all.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a look at the chest seems the quick way to judge a child.

5-Second Recall: Saans poori ek minute gino aur umar ke hisaab se cut-off dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The fast rate that matters is read from the chart of the age of the child.

question: A community nurse who visits the village looks at the graph of the cases of loose stools and sees that all the cases came within a few hours of each other and make a single sharp peak, and the mother of one ill child asks what is happening. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wait for the second peak of cases before a report is sent
option_2: Look for the one food or water that all the cases shared before the illness
option_3: Tell the families that the illness will go away by itself in a few days
option_4: Give the drug for the loose stools to every person of the village
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Look for the one food or water that all the cases shared before the illness

Clinical Rationale: Cases that come within a few hours of each other in one sharp peak point to a common food or water, so the common item of all the cases is looked for at once.

Key Clue: a graph of the cases of loose stools in a village with all the cases within a few hours and one sharp peak

Priority Principle: Public health / Common source

Why Not Others: (a) A wait for the second peak lets the harm of the common source go on; (c) A word that the illness goes by itself leaves the common cause in place; (d) A drug for every person does not remove the common cause.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a drug for all seems the fastest help of a village.

5-Second Recall: Ek hi samay par saare case = ek hi khaane-peene ki cheez dhoondo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The shape of the curve tells the nurse where to look for the cause.

question: A 30-year-old woman in the 34th week of pregnancy who takes a drug for blood pressure is brought to the clinic with giddiness and a pressure of 90/60 mmHg. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the woman to sit up and take a drink of sweet tea
option_2: Give the next dose of the drug and note the pressure on the card
option_3: Hold the drug, lay the woman on her left side and inform the doctor
option_4: Note the pressure and ask the woman to come after two days
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Hold the drug, lay the woman on her left side and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A pressure of 90/60 mmHg with giddiness in a woman who takes a drug for the pressure of pregnancy is too low, so the drug is held, she is laid on the left side and the doctor is told.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman in the 34th week of pregnancy on a drug for blood pressure with giddiness and a pressure of 90/60 mmHg

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Low pressure

Why Not Others: (a) Sitting up drops the pressure further in a woman who is giddy; (b) More of the drug takes the pressure lower and the giddiness deeper; (d) A visit after two days leaves a low pressure without care.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the ordered dose seems the plain duty of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Pregnancy me BP 90/60 aur chakkar = dawa roko, left side letao, doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: A pressure that falls below the normal range is held before the next dose.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A young man of 20 years in a village has NOT slept for four nights and tells the family that he will buy the whole market with money that he does NOT have. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for sleep from the bag of the nurse at once
option_2: Laugh with the man and ask the family to keep him at home
option_3: Stay with the man calmly and take him to the centre for care of the mind
option_4: Tell the family that this state will go away in a few days
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stay with the man calmly and take him to the centre for care of the mind

Clinical Rationale: A young man who does NOT sleep for four nights and talks of money that he does NOT have is in a state of illness, so he is kept calm and taken to the centre at once.

Key Clue: young man of 20 years who has NOT slept for four nights and talks of buying the market with money that he does NOT have

Priority Principle: Safety / Mental health

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet from the bag is given only on the order of a doctor; (b) A laugh at his talk feeds the state of the man; (d) A wait of a few days lets the state of the man go deeper.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the joy of the man seems a happy hour for the family.

5-Second Recall: Chaar raat bina neend aur badi baatein = shaant karo, centre le jao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A state of high joy with no sleep is treated with the same speed as a state of fear.

question: A 5-year-old child in a village has a fever with a swelling of the cheek and the jaw that makes eating painful, and two other children in the lane have the same swelling, and the mother of one of them asks what to do. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the fever to the three children and let them play
option_2: Send the children home from the school of the lane and report the cases as a group
option_3: Put a warm pack on the swelling of the jaw of every child
option_4: Note the swelling in the register and look at the children after a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Send the children home from the school of the lane and report the cases as a group

Clinical Rationale: A fever with a swelling of the jaw in three children of one lane is an illness that spreads from child to child, so the children are kept from the school and the cases are reported as a group.

Key Clue: 5-year-old child with fever and a swelling of the cheek and jaw, and two other children of the lane with the same

Priority Principle: Public health / Group of cases

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet for the fever and play in the lane spread the illness; (c) A warm pack does not stop the spread of the illness; (d) A look after a week is far too late for the children of the lane.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a tablet for the fever seems the whole care of the child.

5-Second Recall: Ek hi gali me teen bachchon ka jaw sooja = school se roko, group me report karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cases of one illness in one lane are reported as a group and not one by one.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 40-year-old man comes to the clinic with a small painless sore on the private part after a stay away from home, and he asks the nurse NOT to tell any person. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Keep the talk private and send the man to the centre for the test and the treatment
option_2: Tell the wife about the sore so that she is NOT harmed
option_3: Put an ointment on the sore and ask him to come after a month
option_4: Tell the man that the sore will go away without any treatment
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the talk private and send the man to the centre for the test and the treatment

Clinical Rationale: A painless sore on the private part is treated at the centre with the talk kept private, and the partner is brought for care through the man and NOT against his wish.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man with a small painless sore on the private part after a stay away from home

Priority Principle: Infection / Private part

Why Not Others: (b) Telling the wife without the wish of the man drives him away from treatment; (c) An ointment and a wait of a month let the sore spread to others; (d) The sore that goes by itself still harms the man and his partner.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because an ointment seems the simple cure of a small sore.

5-Second Recall: Bina dard ka ghaav = private baat rakh kar centre bhejo, ilaaj turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: The partner is brought into care with the help of the client and not by a report.

question: A woman of 30 years in a village with three children and her husband ask the nurse about a method that is permanent. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the woman to try a tablet for a year before the operation
option_2: Tell the woman that the operation is done for the husband alone
option_3: Arrange the operation for the next day without any talk with the family
option_4: Talk with the woman and her husband about the methods and help them to choose
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Talk with the woman and her husband about the methods and help them to choose

Clinical Rationale: A permanent method is chosen by the woman and her husband after talking about the methods, so both are told and are helped to choose the one that fits them.

Key Clue: woman of 30 years in a village with three children who asks about a method that is permanent

Priority Principle: Health promotion / Permanent method

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet for a year is a choice of the couple and not a rule; (b) The operation is done for the woman as well as for the husband; (c) An operation without the talk of the family is not a chosen method.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the operation for the husband seems the common choice.

5-Second Recall: Permanent method = pati-patni dono se baat, dono ke liye rasta hai.

PNC Exam Pearl: The choice of a permanent method is made by the couple together.

question: A nurse who visits the houses of a village is to carry out the spray against the mosquito, and a family asks what it should do before the spray. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Spray the water of the wells of the village with the drug
option_2: Spray the walls of the rooms with the families inside
option_3: Ask the families to take the food and the pots out of the room before the spray
option_4: Ask the families to keep the windows closed for the spray
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Ask the families to take the food and the pots out of the room before the spray

Clinical Rationale: The food and the pots are taken out of the room before the spray, so that the drug of the spray stays off the food of the families.

Key Clue: the spray of the houses of a village against the mosquito

Priority Principle: Procedure / Spray of the houses

Why Not Others: (a) The spray of the walls and the spray of the wells are two different works; (b) A spray with the families inside puts the drug on the skin and the breath; (d) Closed windows hold the drug in the room for hours.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the spray inside seems the fastest work of the day.

5-Second Recall: Spray se pehle khaana aur bartan kamre se bahar.

PNC Exam Pearl: The room is made ready for the spray before the drug is mixed.

question: A boy of 12 years works in a small shop in the village and smokes the bidis that are sold there, and his mother asks the nurse what to do. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet to take away the wish for the bidi
option_2: Tell the mother to punish the boy for the smoking
option_3: Ask the family to keep the boy away from the shop at once
option_4: Talk with the boy about the harm of the bidi and take him to the centre for help
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Talk with the boy about the harm of the bidi and take him to the centre for help

Clinical Rationale: A boy who smokes at 12 years is talked to about the harm of the bidi with care and is taken to the centre where help against the habit is given.

Key Clue: boy of 12 years who works in a small shop and smokes the bidis sold there

Priority Principle: School health / Tobacco

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet does not take away a habit that is built by the day; (b) A punishment drives the habit under the eyes of the family; (c) Away from the shop the boy finds the bidi in other hands.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a punishment seems the fast end of the habit.

5-Second Recall: 12 saal ka bachcha bidi peeta hai = pyaar se samjhao, centre par madad dilao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A habit of tobacco is treated with the help of the family and not with fear.

question: A community nurse finds a 35-year-old man in a village house with stools that look like rice water, and he is very weak with sunken eyes, and the family asks for help. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Start the salt solution at once, send him to the centre and make the water of the house safe
option_2: Give a strong drug to stop the stools and ask the family to watch him
option_3: Ask the family to give him only coconut water for a day
option_4: Note the case in the register and visit the house after two days
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Start the salt solution at once, send him to the centre and make the water of the house safe

Clinical Rationale: Stools that look like rice water with deep weakness point to a disease that spreads by water, so the salt solution is started at once, the man is sent to the centre and the water of the house is made safe.

Key Clue: 35-year-old man with stools like rice water, deep weakness and sunken eyes in a house of a village

Priority Principle: Infection / Water-borne

Why Not Others: (b) A strong drug to stop the stools holds the germ inside the bowel; (c) Coconut water does not replace the water and the salt that is lost; (d) A visit after two days lets the illness spread in the houses of the lane.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a drug to stop the stools seems the FIRST need of the man.

5-Second Recall: Chawal ke paani jaise dast = ORS abhi, centre bhejo, paani saaf karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A stool that looks like rice water is treated with fluid and with clean water for the lane.

question: A community nurse who visits the stone quarry finds that the workers, including a man of 40 years, have a cough for months in a cloud of dust, and his family asks for help. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a syrup for the cough to the workers of the quarry
option_2: Look at the workers for the signs of a disease of the lungs and teach them the use of a mask
option_3: Ask the workers to change their work in the quarry at once
option_4: Note the cough in the register and look at the workers after six months
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Look at the workers for the signs of a disease of the lungs and teach them the use of a mask

Clinical Rationale: Dust of the stone with a cough for months is examined for a disease of the lungs, and the workers are taught to cover the face, because the harm comes back with every day of work.

Key Clue: workers of a stone quarry who work in a cloud of dust with a cough for months

Priority Principle: Occupational health / Lungs

Why Not Others: (a) A syrup for the cough does not take the dust out of the lungs; (c) A change of work is a choice of the workers and not a rule of the nurse; (d) A look after six months lets the harm of the dust go on.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a syrup seems the simple cure of a cough of the work.

5-Second Recall: Patthar ki khan me dhool aur mahino ki khansi = TB ki jaanch aur mask sikhayo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A cough of the work is examined as a harm of the work and not as a common cold.

question: A 25-year-old woman in the 36th week of pregnancy comes to the clinic with swelling of both feet, a gain of two kilograms in a week and a mild headache. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the woman to rest with the feet up and to take less salt
option_2: Tell the woman that a swelling of the feet is common in the last month
option_3: Send the woman to the centre for a pressure and urine test at once
option_4: Note the gain of weight and visit the woman after a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Send the woman to the centre for a pressure and urine test at once

Clinical Rationale: A swelling of both feet with a fast gain of weight and a headache late in pregnancy points to a rise of blood pressure, so the woman is sent for a pressure and urine test at once.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman in the 36th week of pregnancy with swelling of both feet, a gain of two kilograms in a week and a headache

Priority Principle: Mother and fetus / Rise of the pressure

Why Not Others: (a) Rest with less salt helps but does not take the place of a test; (b) A swelling of the feet with a fast gain of weight and a headache is not a common state; (d) A visit after a week lets the rise of the pressure go to a fit.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a swelling of the feet seems a common state of the last month.

5-Second Recall: Pairon ki sujan aur ek hafte me 2 kg wazan = BP-urine jaanch turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: A fast gain of weight is read with the swelling and the headache of the pregnancy.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 50-year-old man comes to the clinic with a wound on the foot that has NOT healed for a month, and he passes a lot of urine and feels thirsty the whole day. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give an ointment for the wound and ask him to come next week
option_2: Test the urine of the man for sugar and send him to the centre
option_3: Ask the man to take more water and to rest the foot
option_4: Tell the man that the wound of the foot will heal by itself
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Test the urine of the man for sugar and send him to the centre

Clinical Rationale: A wound that does NOT heal with much urine and thirst points to sugar in the blood, so the urine is tested and the man is sent to the centre at once.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man with a wound on the foot that has NOT healed for a month, much urine and thirst the whole day

Priority Principle: Screening / Sugar in the blood

Why Not Others: (a) An ointment for the wound leaves the cause behind the wound untouched; (c) More water and rest of the foot do not treat the sugar; (d) A wound that does not heal in a month is a call for a test.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the ointment seems the whole care of a wound of the foot.

5-Second Recall: Mahine bhar na bharne wala ghaav + zyada peshaab = sugar ki jaanch.

PNC Exam Pearl: A wound that does not heal is examined for sugar before a dressing is chosen.

question: A community nurse who visits the village has one ASHA worker with her and four tasks for the day: the weighing of the children, the dressing of a wound, the teaching of a family and the record of the register. Which task should the nurse hand to the ASHA worker FIRST?
option_1: The weighing of the children of the anganwadi with the growth chart
option_2: The dressing of the wound of a client who has an order for it
option_3: The teaching of a family that is to care for a newborn
option_4: The writing of the record of the register of the day
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The weighing of the children of the anganwadi with the growth chart

Clinical Rationale: The weighing of the children with the growth chart is a task that an ASHA worker is trained for, while the wound, the teaching and the record stay with the nurse.

Key Clue: a nurse with one ASHA worker and four tasks: the weighing of the children, a wound, a teaching and the register

Priority Principle: Delegation / Community work

Why Not Others: (b) A wound with an order is dressed by the nurse; (c) The teaching of a family for a newborn needs the knowledge of the nurse; (d) The record of the register is kept by the nurse who gives the care.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because the register seems the work that takes the longest time.

5-Second Recall: Weighing ka kaam ASHA ko do, dawa-teaching khud karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The task is handed to the worker who is trained for it.

question: A 40-year-old man with a fracture of the leg is brought to the clinic with the limb tied to a stick by the family, and the toes are pale. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the man to walk with the stick and test the strength of the leg
option_2: Pull the limb straight and set the bone at the centre
option_3: Tie the limb tighter so that the bone does NOT move on the way
option_4: Keep the limb still as it lies and take away the tight tying of the family
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Keep the limb still as it lies and take away the tight tying of the family

Clinical Rationale: A limb that is tied tight with pale toes is short of blood, so the limb is kept still and the tight tying is taken away at once.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man with a fracture of the leg tied to a stick and toes that are pale

Priority Principle: Emergency / Blood flow of the limb

Why Not Others: (a) A walk on a limb that is broken harms the limb more; (b) A pull on the limb at the centre can harm the vessel and the nerves; (c) A tighter tying stops the flow of blood to the toes.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a tight tying seems the safe hold of a broken limb.

5-Second Recall: Tooti haddi aur safed ungliyan = kas ke bandha hua kholo, hilao mat.

PNC Exam Pearl: The colour and the pulse of the toes decide the hour of the first care.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 55-year-old man of the village had a stroke a week ago, and now he cannot move the left arm and cannot speak clearly, and the family asks for advice. Which advice should the nurse give the family FIRST?
option_1: Ask the man to walk in the courtyard to build strength
option_2: Give water by mouth with a spoon many times a day
option_3: Massage the weak arm with oil every day for strength
option_4: Keep the man on one side, give no fluid by mouth and take him to the centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Keep the man on one side, give no fluid by mouth and take him to the centre

Clinical Rationale: A man who has had a stroke may NOT be able to swallow safely, so he is laid on one side and given nothing by mouth as he is taken to the centre.

Key Clue: man of 55 years a week after a stroke who cannot move the left arm and cannot speak clearly

Priority Principle: ABC / Stroke

Why Not Others: (a) A walk in the courtyard without support brings a fall; (b) Water by mouth in a man who cannot swallow enters the lungs; (c) Massage of the arm does not bring back the power of the brain.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because water by the spoon seems the FIRST care of a weak man.

5-Second Recall: Stroke ke baad nigalna nahi, muh se kuch nahi - side par letao, centre le jao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The swallowing of a client after a stroke is checked before any fluid by mouth.

question: A young man of 25 years in a village who takes a drug for fits has stopped the drug for a month because of the cost, and his family asks the nurse what to do. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a drug of the same group from the bag of the nurse at once
option_2: Ask the family to save money for the drug and start it after a month
option_3: Tell the family that the drug is free at the centre and restart it on the order of the doctor
option_4: Tell the young man to take the drug only on the days of a fit
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Tell the family that the drug is free at the centre and restart it on the order of the doctor

Clinical Rationale: The drugs for fits are free at the centre, so the family is told and the drug is restarted on the order of the doctor, because a stop of a month brings the fits back.

Key Clue: young man of 25 years who stopped the drug for fits for a month because of the cost

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Long treatment

Why Not Others: (a) A drug from the bag is given only on the order of a doctor; (b) A month of saving lets the fits start again in the man; (d) A drug taken only on the days of a fit keeps no guard against the fits.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because money seems the wall that the family cannot cross.

5-Second Recall: Fits ki dawa centre par muft milti hai - band ki gayi dawa wapas shuru karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The cost of a long treatment is the common reason for a stop and is met by the programme.

question: In a village, 50 children were in a room with a child who had chickenpox, and 20 of them fell ill after two weeks, and the mother of one of them asks the nurse what this means. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet against the virus to the 30 children who are well
option_2: Work out the rate of the illness among the children and report the group of cases
option_3: Close the school of the village for the next two weeks
option_4: Note the names of the 20 ill children in the register alone
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Work out the rate of the illness among the children and report the group of cases

Clinical Rationale: Twenty ill children among fifty exposed children give a rate of forty per cent, and the rate with the report of the group is the FIRST work of the nurse.

Key Clue: 50 children in a room with a child with chickenpox and 20 of them ill after two weeks

Priority Principle: Public health / Rate of the illness

Why Not Others: (a) A drug against the virus is not given to every child who is well; (c) A closed school does not treat the children who are already ill; (d) A note of the names without the rate says nothing of the spread.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a closed school seems the sure stop of the spread.

5-Second Recall: 50 me se 20 bimaar = attack rate 40%, rate nikaalo aur report karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The number of the ill among the exposed is worked out before the report is sent.

question: A 45-year-old man comes to the clinic with a pain in the back that runs down the leg after he lifted a heavy load, and now he cannot lift the foot up. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Keep the man on a hard bed without a pillow and send him to the centre
option_2: Ask the man to bend the back and touch the toes to loosen it
option_3: Put a warm pack on the back and ask him to walk about
option_4: Give a tablet for the pain and ask him to lift no load for a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the man on a hard bed without a pillow and send him to the centre

Clinical Rationale: A pain that runs down the leg with a foot that cannot be lifted points to a press on the nerve, so the man is kept straight on a hard bed and is sent to the centre.

Key Clue: 45-year-old man with pain in the back that runs down the leg after lifting a load and a foot that cannot be lifted

Priority Principle: Emergency / Press on the nerve

Why Not Others: (b) A bend of the back presses the nerve more; (c) A warm pack and a walk do not take the press off the nerve; (d) A tablet for the pain hides the loss of the power of the foot.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a warm pack seems the relief of a back that pains.

5-Second Recall: Kamar ka dard pair tak aur paon nahi uthta = hard bed, hilao mat, centre bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A loss of the power of the foot with a pain of the back is a nerve in danger.

question: A boy of 10 years is pulled out of a pond in the village and is NOT breathing with a blue face, and his mother calls the nurse. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Hold the boy up by the legs to let the water run out
option_2: Open the airway, take the water out of the mouth and start the breaths at once
option_3: Press the belly of the boy hard to push the water out
option_4: Take the boy to the house of the family and wait for the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Open the airway, take the water out of the mouth and start the breaths at once

Clinical Rationale: A boy who is NOT breathing with a blue face is given the airway and the breaths at once, because the air that is short matters more than the water in the belly.

Key Clue: boy of 10 years pulled out of a pond who is NOT breathing and has a blue face

Priority Principle: ABC / Drowning

Why Not Others: (a) A hold by the legs lets the vomit enter the airway; (c) A press on the belly brings the water of the stomach up into the airway; (d) A wait for the doctor in a house loses the minutes that matter.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the water in the boy seems the FIRST thing to take out.

5-Second Recall: Paani me dubne ke baad saans nahi = air way kholo, saans do, turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: The airway is opened before any water is pushed out of the belly.

question: A 25-year-old woman in the sixth month of pregnancy comes to the clinic and says that after a week of iron and folic acid tablets the stool has become black and hard. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a strong drug to open the bowel along with the iron
option_2: Stop the iron tablets till the stool becomes normal again
option_3: Tell her that the black stool is common with iron and to take more water and greens
option_4: Change the iron tablets to a syrup of the same iron at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Tell her that the black stool is common with iron and to take more water and greens

Clinical Rationale: A black stool is common with iron tablets and a hard stool is helped by more water and green vegetables, so the woman is told that the iron goes on.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman in the sixth month of pregnancy on iron tablets with a black and hard stool

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Side effect

Why Not Others: (a) A strong drug for the bowel without an order is not given by the nurse; (b) A stop of the iron takes away the guard against a low blood count; (d) A syrup of iron brings the same side effect and wastage.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a strong drug for the bowel seems the fast ease of the woman.

5-Second Recall: Iron se kala stool normal - paani aur hari sabzi badhao, dawa band nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The black colour of the stool is the iron and not blood.

question: A mother brings the report of her 2-year-old child who is weak, and the report shows a haemoglobin of 7 g/dL. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the child buffalo milk many times a day
option_2: Give a syrup of the vitamins alone and ask the mother to come after a month
option_3: Tell the mother that a low blood count is common in children of this age
option_4: Start the iron syrup with advice on food and send the child to the centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Start the iron syrup with advice on food and send the child to the centre

Clinical Rationale: A haemoglobin of 7 g/dL with weakness is a low blood count, so the iron syrup with advice on food is started and the child is sent to the centre for the cause.

Key Clue: 2-year-old child who is weak and a report of haemoglobin 7 g/dL

Priority Principle: Child health / Low blood count

Why Not Others: (a) Milk alone gives little iron and takes away the wish for food; (b) A syrup of the vitamins alone does not build the blood; (c) A haemoglobin of 7 g/dL is not called common at this age.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because vitamins seem the whole care of a weak child.

5-Second Recall: Hb 7 aur kamzori = iron syrup aur khane ki salah, centre bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The report of the blood is read with the food of the child, because iron needs food and light.

question: A 30-year-old woman in a village has had no child in five years of marriage, and the family blames her and asks the nurse to help. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Talk with both the woman and her husband and send both to the centre for tests
option_2: Send the woman alone to the city hospital for a test of the uterus
option_3: Ask the family to wait for two more years before any test
option_4: Give the woman a drug to build her strength
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Talk with both the woman and her husband and send both to the centre for tests

Clinical Rationale: The cause of no child in five years may lie with either partner, so both are talked to with care and both are sent to the centre for tests.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman with no child in five years of marriage and a family that blames her

Priority Principle: Maternal care / Both partners

Why Not Others: (b) The test of the woman alone leaves the man out of the search for the cause; (c) A wait of two more years takes away the years of the woman; (d) A drug for strength does not treat the cause of no child.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the blame of the family turns the eyes to the woman.

5-Second Recall: Paanch saal me bachcha nahi = dono partner ki jaanch, sirf aurat par dosh nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: Both the partners are examined when a child does not come.

question: A 25-year-old woman in the tenth week of pregnancy comes to the clinic after vomiting many times a day for four days, and she cannot keep any food and her mouth is dry. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give small sips of the salt solution and send her to the centre
option_2: Ask the woman to take dry toast and to rest for a day
option_3: Give a strong drug to stop the vomiting at once
option_4: Tell the woman that vomiting in the early months is common
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give small sips of the salt solution and send her to the centre

Clinical Rationale: Vomiting many times for four days with a dry mouth brings a loss of water, so small sips of the salt solution are given and the woman is sent for fluid into the vein.

Key Clue: 25-year-old woman in the tenth week of pregnancy with vomiting for four days, a dry mouth and no food kept

Priority Principle: Early pregnancy / Loss of water

Why Not Others: (b) Dry toast and rest do not replace the water that is lost; (c) A strong drug to stop the vomiting is given only on the order of a doctor; (d) Vomiting that keeps no food for days is not common in early pregnancy.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because the vomiting of early pregnancy seems a common state.

5-Second Recall: Chaar din ulti aur sookha muh = ORS ke ghunt, vein me fluid ke liye bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The vomiting of pregnancy is watched for the loss of water and the weight.

question: A nurse visits the house of a 40-year-old man who is on the drugs for tuberculosis, and the house has four other members. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a mask to every member of the family to wear in the house
option_2: Tell the family why the visit is made and ask for their help with the tests
option_3: Tell the family to keep the man in a room away from the others
option_4: Note the names of the family in the register and visit after a month
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Tell the family why the visit is made and ask for their help with the tests

Clinical Rationale: The purpose of the visit is told to the family and their help is asked for, so that the family members come for the test of the disease with trust.

Key Clue: a house of a man of 40 years on the drugs for tuberculosis with four other members

Priority Principle: Public health / Family of a case

Why Not Others: (a) A mask in the house is no guard for the days and the nights of the family; (c) A room apart brings shame and hides the members from the test; (d) A visit after a month lets the disease show itself in the family.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a mask seems the simple guard of a family.

5-Second Recall: TB ke ghar me pehle parivar se baat karo, phir sabki jaanch karwao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The family of a case is brought for the test with trust and not with fear.

question: A family in a village eats rice with a thin soup of pulse and takes no green leaf or fruit, and their 4-year-old child cannot see well in the evening. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the family a tin of milk powder for the child
option_2: Give the child more rice at every meal for strength
option_3: Give vitamin A to the child and teach the family the use of green leaves and fruit
option_4: Ask the family to take the child to the city hospital for the eyes
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Give vitamin A to the child and teach the family the use of green leaves and fruit

Clinical Rationale: A child who cannot see well in the evening with a diet of rice and thin pulse needs vitamin A at once, and the family is taught to use green leaves and fruit in the food.

Key Clue: 4-year-old child who cannot see well in the evening in a family that eats rice and thin pulse with no green leaf

Priority Principle: Nutrition / Lack of vitamin A

Why Not Others: (a) A tin of milk powder does not give the vitamin that the eyes need; (b) More rice gives energy but no vitamin A for the eyes; (d) A city hospital is far for a state that is met at the centre.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because more rice seems enough food for a child.

5-Second Recall: Raat me nahi dikhta = vitamin A abhi, hari sabzi aur phal sikhayo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The food of the family is changed as well as the vitamin that is given.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 40-year-old woman in a village has a swelling in front of the neck, and her 6-year-old child is short for the age with a dull face. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the family that the swelling of the neck runs in families
option_2: Give the woman a tablet of iron and ask her to come after a month
option_3: Ask the family to give the child more milk in the day
option_4: Tell the family to use iodised salt and send both to the centre for a test
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Tell the family to use iodised salt and send both to the centre for a test

Clinical Rationale: A swelling in front of the neck with a child who is short and dull points to a lack of iodine, so the family is told to use iodised salt and both are sent for a test.

Key Clue: 40-year-old woman with a swelling in front of the neck and a child of 6 years who is short and dull

Priority Principle: Public health / Lack of iodine

Why Not Others: (a) A swelling of the neck and a dull child are not a family trait; (b) A tablet of iron does not treat a lack of iodine; (c) Milk in the day does not give the iodine that is missing.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because milk seems the food that builds a short child.

5-Second Recall: Gale me soojan aur mand buddhi bachcha = iodised namak, jaanch ke liye bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Iodised salt guards the neck and the mind of the coming child.

question: A mother of a 2-year-old child in a village gives buffalo milk in a bottle at night and washes the bottle only with the water of the pump. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Give the milk with a cup and a spoon and wash the cup with clean water
option_2: Wash the bottle with the water of the pump and boil it once a week
option_3: Give the bottle with a longer nipple so that the milk comes fast
option_4: Stop the buffalo milk at night and give only breast milk
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give the milk with a cup and a spoon and wash the cup with clean water

Clinical Rationale: The milk is given with a cup and a spoon with a clean wash of the cup, because a bottle that is washed in the pump water carries the germs of the loose stools.

Key Clue: mother of a 2-year-old child who gives buffalo milk in a bottle at night washed only with pump water

Priority Principle: Child health / Feeding

Why Not Others: (b) A weekly boil leaves the bottle with germs on the other days; (c) A longer nipple and a fast flow bring choking and more infection; (d) A stop of the milk at night does not teach the clean way to give it.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a longer nipple seems the easy way to feed a child.

5-Second Recall: Bottle ki jagah cup-chammach, aur bartan saaf paani se dhoyo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A cup and a spoon are cleaner than a bottle from the first month.

question: A 60-year-old man at home who is on bed rest after a long illness has a dry mouth with a thick coating on the tongue and a bad smell, and the family asks what can be done. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a strong wash of the mouth with spirit and water
option_2: Clean the mouth with soft swabs and clean water and look at the tongue in good light
option_3: Ask the man to take a lot of water to wash the mouth inside
option_4: Give a tablet for the bad smell and note the state after a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clean the mouth with soft swabs and clean water and look at the tongue in good light

Clinical Rationale: A dry mouth with a thick coating is cleaned with soft swabs and clean water, and the tongue is examined in good light, because a mouth that is NOT cleaned brings sores and infection.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man on bed rest with a dry mouth, a thick coating on the tongue and a bad smell

Priority Principle: Mouth care / Comfort

Why Not Others: (a) A spirit wash in the mouth harms the skin inside and dries it more; (c) A lot of water by mouth is a risk in a man on bed rest after a long illness; (d) A tablet for the smell does not clean the mouth of the man.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a strong wash seems the sure cleaning of a dirty mouth.

5-Second Recall: Muh ki safai naram swab aur saaf paani se - spirit nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: Mouth care is given with the head turned to one side and the swabs soft.

question: A family in a village keeps the cattle in the same room where the family sleeps, and a 40-year-old man of the house has a fever that comes and goes with pain in the joints. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the family to keep the windows of the room open at night
option_2: Give a tablet for the fever to every member of the family
option_3: Tell the family to shelter the cattle apart from the room where the family sleeps
option_4: Note the case in the register and visit the house after two weeks
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Tell the family to shelter the cattle apart from the room where the family sleeps

Clinical Rationale: Cattle in the room of the family with a fever and pain in the joints point to an illness that passes from the animals, so the cattle are sheltered apart and the members of the house are examined.

Key Clue: family of a village that keeps the cattle in the room where it sleeps and a case of fever with joint pain

Priority Principle: Public health / Animals and men

Why Not Others: (a) An open window does not keep the germs of the animals out of the room; (b) A tablet for every member does not part the cattle from the family; (d) A visit after two weeks lets the illness go round the house.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tablet for all seems the fast end of the fever.

5-Second Recall: Janwar aur parivar ek hi kamre me = alag rakho, ghar walon ki jaanch karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: An illness of the cattle is examined as an illness of the family that lives with them.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 55-year-old man comes to the clinic with a cough for years, swelling of both legs that keeps the mark of a finger, and he sleeps with three pillows. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put a warm pack on the legs and ask him to take less salt
option_2: Give a water tablet from the bag of the nurse and let him rest at home
option_3: Ask the man to walk about the village to bring the swelling down
option_4: Keep the man propped up, give oxygen if it is near and send him to the hospital
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Keep the man propped up, give oxygen if it is near and send him to the hospital

Clinical Rationale: A long cough with swelling of both legs and a breath that is short on lying flat points to a failing heart, so the man is propped up and sent to the hospital at once.

Key Clue: 55-year-old man with a cough for years, swelling of both legs that keeps the mark of a finger and three pillows at night

Priority Principle: ABC / Failing heart

Why Not Others: (a) A warm pack and less salt do not treat a failing heart; (b) A water tablet from the bag without an order and rest at home leave the heart without care; (c) A walk of the village takes the breath that the man does not have.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a walk seems the way to bring a swelling down.

5-Second Recall: Lambe khansi, pairon ki sujan, teen takiye = baithao, hospital turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: The number of pillows at night tells how short the breath of the man is.

question: A nurse who visits the village is asked to plan the care of the crowd at a festival that will bring many persons together for two days, and a family asks what will be done. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Arrange a dose of the drug against the loose stools for every visitor
option_2: Ask the families of the village to keep their children at home
option_3: Arrange safe water and clean food stalls and keep a post of FIRST aid ready
option_4: Note the number of the visitors in the register of the centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Arrange safe water and clean food stalls and keep a post of FIRST aid ready

Clinical Rationale: A crowd of two days is guarded by safe water, clean food stalls and a post of FIRST aid that is ready before the FIRST visitor comes.

Key Clue: a festival of a village that brings many persons together for two days

Priority Principle: Public health / Crowd

Why Not Others: (a) A drug for every visitor is no guard against a food-borne illness; (b) A word to keep the children at home takes away the joy of the festival; (d) A note of the number does not stop the illness of a crowd.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a drug for all seems the sure guard of a crowd.

5-Second Recall: Mela se pehle saaf paani, saaf khaana, first-aid post - yahi plan.

PNC Exam Pearl: A crowd is guarded by the water and the food and not by a drug.

question: A 30-year-old man in a village has yellow eyes with a fever and a poor appetite, and the family takes the water of the canal for drinking. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the case in the register and look at the family after a month
option_2: Give a tablet for the fever and ask the family to keep the man apart
option_3: Ask the family to give the man only sugar cane juice
option_4: Send the blood of the man for a test and tell the family to boil the drinking water
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Send the blood of the man for a test and tell the family to boil the drinking water

Clinical Rationale: Yellow eyes with a fever and drinking water that is NOT safe point to an illness of the liver that spreads by water, so the blood is sent for a test and the family is told to boil the water.

Key Clue: 30-year-old man with yellow eyes and a fever and a family that drinks the water of the canal

Priority Principle: Public health / Water of the canal

Why Not Others: (a) A look after a month lets the illness spread in the lanes; (b) A tablet for the fever and a room apart do not clean the water of the canal; (c) Sugar cane juice gives energy but does not treat the liver.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because sugar cane juice seems the care of a weak liver.

5-Second Recall: Peeli aankhein aur nadi ka paani = khoon ki jaanch, paani ubaal ke peena.

PNC Exam Pearl: Safe water of a lane is planned with the case of a fever of the liver.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 30-year-old man who has taken a drug for fits for two years and has had no fit for a year stopped the drug himself last week, and his family brings him to the clinic with two fits in a day. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Send the man to the centre at once and tell the family that the drug is NOT stopped by the man
option_2: Give a double dose of the drug from the bag and let him rest at home
option_3: Ask the family to tie the hands of the man during the fits
option_4: Note the two fits on the card and ask him to come after a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Send the man to the centre at once and tell the family that the drug is NOT stopped by the man

Clinical Rationale: A stop of the drug for fits by the man himself brings the fits back, so he is sent to the centre at once and the family is told that the drug is changed only by the doctor.

Key Clue: 30-year-old man who stopped the drug for fits himself last week and now has two fits in a day

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Stop of a drug

Why Not Others: (b) A double dose from the bag without an order is not given by the nurse; (c) A tie of the hands during the fits harms the man and does not stop them; (d) A week of waiting brings more fits to the man.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a tie of the hands seems the safe care during a fit.

5-Second Recall: Fits ki dawa khud band = turant centre bhejo, dawa sirf doctor badlega.

PNC Exam Pearl: A drug of the fits is stopped slowly and only on the order of the doctor.

question: A mother brings her 3-year-old child to the clinic and says the child was given a tablet for the pain from the shop two hours ago and is now sleepy with slow breathing. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a drink of milk to the child and watch him for an hour
option_2: Take the child to the hospital at once with the packet of the tablet
option_3: Give a syrup to wake the child and send him home to rest
option_4: Ask the mother about the other children of the house
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Take the child to the hospital at once with the packet of the tablet

Clinical Rationale: A child who is sleepy with slow breathing after a tablet from the shop is taken to the hospital at once with the packet, so that the drug is known and the care is begun.

Key Clue: 3-year-old child who took a tablet for the pain from the shop two hours ago and now is sleepy with slow breathing

Priority Principle: Drug safety / Poison of a drug

Why Not Others: (a) A drink of milk does not take away a drug that is already in the body; (c) A syrup to wake the child hides the state of the poison; (d) The talk about the other children can come after the child is moved.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a drink of milk seems the FIRST care of a poison.

5-Second Recall: Dukaan ki goli ke baad neend aur dheemi saans = packet le kar turant hospital.

PNC Exam Pearl: The packet of the drug goes with the child so that the hospital knows the poison.

question: A 35-year-old woman in a village cooks on a wood fire in a small room with the door closed and has had a cough with a wheeze for many weeks, and her family asks what can be done. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Look at her breathing and teach the family about the smoke of the chulha and the open door
option_2: Give a syrup for the cough and ask her to come after a month
option_3: Ask the woman to take a drug for the cough from the shop
option_4: Tell the family that the cough will go with the change of the season
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Look at her breathing and teach the family about the smoke of the chulha and the open door

Clinical Rationale: Smoke of the wood fire in a closed room harms the lungs, so the breathing is examined and the family is taught to cook with the smoke going out of the room.

Key Clue: 35-year-old woman who cooks on a wood fire in a small closed room and has a cough with a wheeze for weeks

Priority Principle: Occupational health / Smoke of the house

Why Not Others: (b) A syrup for the cough does not take the smoke out of the room; (c) A drug from the shop without a look at the breathing hides the harm; (d) A cough of the smoke does not go with the change of the season.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a syrup seems the whole care of a cough.

5-Second Recall: Band kamre me chulha aur khansi = dhuan bahar nikalo, saans dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The smoke of the house is a cause of a cough that the family can set right.

question: A 30-year-old woman in a village has a swelling of the leg with a history of passing a thin worm in the stool, and two others in her family have the same swelling. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a tablet for the worms to the woman alone and note the swelling
option_2: Take the blood of the three of them at night for a test and look at the whole house
option_3: Put a tight band on the leg and ask the woman to rest on the bed
option_4: Note the swelling in the register and look at the house after a month
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Take the blood of the three of them at night for a test and look at the whole house

Clinical Rationale: A swelling of the leg with a worm in the stool and other cases in the house points to an illness of the worms of the blood, so the blood is taken at night and the whole house is examined.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman with a swelling of the leg, a worm in the stool and two others of the house with the same swelling

Priority Principle: Public health / Worms of the blood

Why Not Others: (a) A tablet for the worms of the bowel does not treat the worms of the blood; (c) A tight band on a leg that is swollen harms the skin; (d) A look after a month lets the illness go round the house.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a tablet for the worms seems the cure of the worm in the stool.

5-Second Recall: Pair ki sujan aur mal me kida = raat me khoon ki jaanch, poora ghar dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The worms of the blood are looked for at night when they move in the blood.

question: A 70-year-old man who lives alone is found by a neighbour very weak and NOT able to stand, and the house has had no food for two days and no water in the pot, and his family lives far away. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the neighbour to bring the food to the man every day
option_2: Give a large meal of rice and pulse at once for strength
option_3: Give a drink with sugar and salt and take him to the centre with a look at the house
option_4: Note the state of the man and ask the family to come after a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Give a drink with sugar and salt and take him to the centre with a look at the house

Clinical Rationale: A man who is very weak with no food and no water for two days is given a drink with sugar and salt and is taken to the centre, and the house is examined for the reasons behind it.

Key Clue: 70-year-old man who lives alone, is very weak and cannot stand, with no food for two days and no water in the pot

Priority Principle: Care of the old / Safety

Why Not Others: (a) A word to the neighbour does not treat the state of the man today; (b) A large meal at once cannot be taken by a man who is very weak; (d) A wait of a week with no food and no water can kill the man.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the neighbour seems the care of the man in the lane.

5-Second Recall: Do din bina khaane-peene ka budha aadmi = meetha-namkeen paani, centre le jao.

PNC Exam Pearl: An old person who lives alone is examined for the house as well as the body.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse opens a sub-centre in the morning and has four tasks: the cold box of the vaccine, the register of the cases, the dressing of a wound and the crowd of persons who wait, among them a mother with her child. Which task should the nurse do FIRST?
option_1: Look at the crowd of persons and send the simple cases to the desk
option_2: Write the register of the cases of the day at the desk
option_3: Dress the wound of the person who has waited the longest
option_4: Look at the cold box and its temperature before the hours of the vaccine
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Look at the cold box and its temperature before the hours of the vaccine

Clinical Rationale: The cold box and its temperature are examined FIRST, because the vaccine that has taken heat is spoiled and the whole session of the day is lost.

Key Clue: a sub-centre to be opened in the morning with a cold box, a register, a wound and a crowd of persons who wait

Priority Principle: Management / Cold chain

Why Not Others: (a) The crowd is examined after the cold box of the centre is safe; (b) The register of the cases is written after the cold box is examined; (c) The wound is dressed after the work of the vaccine is set right.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the person who has waited seems the FIRST duty of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Sub-centre kholte hi pehle cold box aur temperature dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The work of the cold chain comes before the work of the desk.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).
